creatures.loreNote: Folklore translates Sluagh's Collector/judge and parasite/sower function rather than creates it: this ancient cosmic Wyrdkin persists through Gibbets, execution hills, dissolved records, and fog currents carrying unconfessed last words and is not assumed to be Keth-Amar's offspring.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A possible ancient cosmic carrion-memory swarm that uses raven forms, or a local colony assembled by Wyrd around the final thoughts of executed people. It is not a native Frostwood raven species.
loreCanon.function: It circles execution sites, trades secrets, and spreads identity-erasing panic through a coordinated raven swarm.
loreCanon.values: Unconfessed secrets and the memory of the executed; its agency is collective and argumentative rather than mindless.
loreCanon.folklore: A death-crow swarm and whispered last confession are local camouflage and tactical tells. Executions supplied food and an anchor, not necessarily the species' origin.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding supplied more crossroads and political executions; First Cracks made warm routes crowded enough for a cosmic memory swarm to establish a colony.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Ancient Cosmic Wyrdkin versus local Wyrd colony remains unresolved; do not classify every native raven or death-omen as Sluagh.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether a cosmic swarm arrived first and used the Gallow-Wyrd as camouflage, or whether Keth-Amar directly generated this colony from local death residue.
loreCanon.cosmicProvenance: Working hypothesis: a Between swarm that feeds on last signals, dying minds, and discarded identity. Its relationship to Keth-Amar may be ecological rather than genealogical.
loreCanon.wyrdFunction: Collector/judge and parasite/sower; it harvests identity residue and turns records of punishment into a spreading nest.
loreCanon.anchor: Gibbets, execution hills, dissolved records, and fog currents carrying unconfessed last words.
loreCanon.kethRelationship: It may follow Keth-Amar's wake, be directed toward Viridane evidence, or simply exploit the same memory fracture. Direct generation is unconfirmed.
loreCanon.independence: The swarm speaks as a chorus and can trade secrets without an active command. It may form a faction around the memories it has collected.
loreCanon.countermeasure: Free or name the trapped voices, close the execution-site anchor, preserve redundant records, and separate the Wyrd swarm from any native ravens.

folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Gallow-Wyrd / Raven-Swarm (Germanic/Grimm folklore):** Spectral crows that gather around execution sites, carrying away the final words and confessions of the hanged.; **Sluagh-Birds (Celtic folklore):** Restless souls of the dead who take the form of black birds, flying in massive, noisy flocks to gather those who die alone.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Crossroads-Fiend:** They nest in ancient crossroads, execution hills, and misty ravines in Frostwood Reach. They gather around crossroads gibbets, preventing travelers from crossing and feeding on their names and memories. **The Archive Threat:** Regarded as harbingers of death by the locals. Scribes organize hunts to disperse them when they gather near archive towers, as their ash-shroud and pecking can dissolve books and journals.

creatures.name: Wildejagd
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Sluagh
creatures.origin: Descending from the Florae Sluagh, the host of the restless dead, and the Skald Wild Hunt or W,tende Heer, this phantom ridership is a collective manifestation of the forgotten. It represents the ultimate terror of historical erasure, riding through the sky to claim the names of the living.
creatures.nature: This entity is a massive, undulating cloud composed of dozens of twisted, wraith-like riders fused together, moving in sudden, coordinated formations like a flock of starlings. It trails shreds of paper and ink droplets that fall like black snow, accompanied by the spectral sound of horse hooves echoing like slamming doors. Dozens of pale, screaming mouths open and close across its surface, each whispering the names of forgotten ancestors whose records were eaten by the fog.
creatures.habitat: It rides through the night skies during dense fog-storms, circling high above archive towers and fading settlements.
creatures.combat: 390 HP. Archive-Storm (AoE 40 ft, DC 15 SPI or 3d6 psychic + lose one lineage-level memory). Page-Rain (ranged, 2d6 slashing + DC 14 AGI or restrained by paper 1 round). Name-Whisper (passive: whispers forgotten ancestor names; DC 14 SPI or charmed, walking toward the entity). Absorb-Identity (special: when a target loses their last memory to fog within 30 ft, the Sluagh absorbs them, gaining +20 HP). Vulnerable to radiant.
creatures.depth: The Wildejagd raids Greymark's archive towers, tearing down lineage-tapestries to consume the recorded history of entire bloodlines. They also circle those on the verge of total memory-collapse, waiting for their last thoughts to fade so they can absorb the empty shell of identity and add a new rider to their host. Scribes organize desperate hunts to protect their archives, hiring brave parties to retrieve the lost pages and components left in the ride's wake.
hooks: A rumor spreads of a Sluagh spotted near the area.
Adventurers need a component from a Sluagh to complete their quest.
creatures.description: A spectral cloud of fused, wraith-like riders that raids archive towers to devour recorded histories and absorb fading minds.
creatures.heritage: This native or native-adjacent collective wild-hunt phenomenon predates the Great Binding. Rooted in Thalren + Skaldic folklore, the myth of Sluagh originally served as a way for the community to rationalize the forces described in local tales: "Descending from the Skaldic Sluagh, the host of the restless dead, and the Thalren Wild Hunt or W�tende Heer, this phantom ridership is a collective manifestation of the forgotten.". This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It follows memory-collapse, raids records, and marks settlements whose dead or histories have been denied proper passage

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Wildejagd's native baseline rather than creates it: a native or native-adjacent collective wild-hunt phenomenon, possibly a host of dead riders bound to forgotten routes; any Wyrd change belongs to an individual or branch.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native or native-adjacent collective wild-hunt phenomenon, possibly a host of dead riders bound to forgotten routes; the present Sluagh descent needs separation.
loreCanon.function: It follows memory-collapse, raids records, and marks settlements whose dead or histories have been denied proper passage.
loreCanon.values: The memory of the forgotten and the right of the dead to be named.
loreCanon.folklore: Riders in a storm, archive raids, and a final hunt are the reliable pattern. It may be a real host, not merely a fear manifestation.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding created the long darkness and house erasure politics; First Cracks made archive towers and warm settlements visible targets.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Could be a native death-host later infected by Sluagh/Wyrd. Keep `HYBRID-REVIEW` until the native riders and invasive swarm are disentangled.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether the hunt has individual riders with agency or one collective will.

folkloreInspiration.primaryMyth: Sluagh (Celtic/Irish folklore) & The Wild Hunt / Wütende Heer (Germanic folklore)
folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Sluagh (Celtic/Irish folklore):** The host of the unfairy dead  -  restless spirits who fly through the night sky in flocks, trying to steal the souls of the dying before they can reach the afterlife.; **The Wild Hunt / Wütende Heer (Germanic folklore):** A spectral procession of ghostly hunters and hounds that rides across the night sky, foretelling war, plague, or the death of those who witness it.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Archive-Storm:** The Wildejagd descends on Greymark's archive-towers during the thickest fog-nights, attempting to physically tear pages from the great lineage-tapestries. Each page they consume erases an entire bloodline's recorded history. **The Dying-Vigil:** They gather around those on the verge of total memory-collapse, circling like vultures. When the last memory dissolves, the Wildejagd absorbs the empty husk of identity, adding another silent rider to its host.

creatures.name: Fuath
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Fuath
creatures.origin: Tracing its lineage to the Skaldic Florae Fuath and the Skald Nixie, this water spirit is a personification of the deceptive depths. It feeds on the desperation of the forgetful, using their own lost identities as bait to lure them into the dark waters.
creatures.nature: This pale, slender figure appears to stand waist-deep in dark peat-pools, its body entirely translucent so that murky water and floating algae are visible through its skin. It is wrapped in a shimmering film of surface tension that reflects fog-light like oil on water, with long, kelp-like hair extending in all directions. While it seems beautiful from a distance, its features are fluid and constantly shifting, and its eyes are bottomless pools of dark water.
creatures.habitat: It waits in the stagnant peat-pools and boggy lakes that dot the lowlands of Frostwood Reach.
creatures.combat: 90 HP. Pool-Song (AoE 30 ft, DC 13 SPI or compelled to walk toward the pool). Memory-Restore (special: temporarily restores one precious memory to lure the target; this is the bait). Dissolve (1 AP: becomes indistinguishable from pool-water, gaining full concealment). Kelp-Grasp (melee, +4 to hit, DC 13 AGI or grappled and pulled underwater). Vulnerable to lightning.
creatures.depth: The Fuath sings a resonant hum that echoes through the fog, bringing to mind the listener's most cherished, forgotten memories to draw them into the water. Once a victim wades in, the spirit dissolves into the pool, drowning the traveler and sinking their memories into the sediment where they compact into peat over centuries. Communities hire adventurers to search for these spirits to recover lost relatives or harvest their memory-infused water.
hooks: A rumor spreads of a Fuath spotted near the area.
Adventurers need a component from a Fuath to complete their quest.
creatures.description: A translucent water spirit that lures travelers into peat pools by singing songs that recall their most precious memories.
creatures.heritage: This native peat-water singer and boundary spirit predates the Great Binding. Rooted in Thalren + Skaldic folklore, the myth of Fuath originally served as a way for the community to rationalize the forces described in local tales: "Tracing its lineage to the Skaldic Skaldic Fuath and the Thalren Nixie, this water spirit is a personification of the deceptive depths.". This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It protects a pool, recycles drowned memory, and lures only those who violate a water boundary or ignore a warning

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Fuath rather than creates it: a native peat-water singer and boundary spirit, older than the Frostwood fog and not dependent on Wyrd; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native peat-water singer and boundary spirit, older than the Frostwood fog and not dependent on Wyrd.
loreCanon.function: It protects a pool, recycles drowned memory, and lures only those who violate a water boundary or ignore a warning.
loreCanon.values: Water depth, drowned remains, and the right of the pool to remain unentered.
loreCanon.folklore: Song, cherished-memory lure, and dissolution into water are true encounter signs. The memory is bait because it knows the listener, not because a rumor built it.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: Cold preserved pools and reduced river flow; First Cracks created warm pools with more traffic and more boundary disputes.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native water spirit. A Wyrd copy might use stolen memories as bait, but Fuath are not Wyrdspawn.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether Fuath can rescue a respectful swimmer and what they do with the memories they collect.

folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Fuath (Celtic/Scottish folklore):** A generic term for water-spirits and lake-monsters  -  dangerous, ambivalent entities that drag swimmers beneath dark Highland lochs.; **Nixie/Nix (Germanic folklore):** A river-spirit that appears as a beautiful human to lure victims to the water's edge. Some Nixies are benign; most drown those who follow them.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Pool-Singer:** Fuaths stand at the edge of deep peat-pools and sing a low, resonant hum that carries through the fog. The song does not charm  -  instead, it temporarily restores a memory of something precious, drawing the listener toward the pool to reclaim it. **The Memory-Sinker:** When a victim wades in, the Fuath dissolves, becoming indistinguishable from the pool-water. The victim sinks, and the pool absorbs their memories as sediment  -  layers of stolen identities compacting into peat over centuries.

creatures.name: Grogoch
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Grogoch
creatures.origin: Derived from the Florae Grogoch, a helpful yet reclusive hedge-spirit, and the Skald Erdm,nnlein, the industrious little men of the earth, this creature is a master of the soil. It works in the dark beneath the forest floor, maintaining a hidden agricultural network that sustains the region's inhabitants.
creatures.nature: This three-foot-tall biped resembles a walking haystack, covered in dreadlocks of ironwood-moss and matted animal fur. Two short, muscular arms extend from its bulk, holding a small spade made from a sharpened elk shoulder-blade. Its face is almost entirely obscured by hair, showing only a broad nose and beady, black eyes, and its wide mouth is filled with flat, stone teeth.
creatures.habitat: It lives in clean, root-lined burrow systems dug beneath the ironwood forests, ventilated by small, hidden air vents.
creatures.combat: 75 HP. Spade-Strike (melee, +4 to hit, 1d6+2 slashing). Tunnel-Network (passive: knows and can navigate all underground tunnels within 1 mile). Secret-Toll (special: demands one personal secret for passage through a tunnel; refuses to repeat or use the secret). Root-Tender (passive: nearby edible root-plants grow at double rate). Vulnerable to fire.
creatures.depth: Grogochs cultivate vast gardens of edible ironwood-roots and frost-tubers, which serve as a crucial food supply for local villages. They also maintain a network of subterranean tunnels that allow travelers to bypass the memory-fog entirely, demanding a secret as payment for using these safe passages. Villages often hire adventurers to trade with them or protect their burrows from surface predators.
hooks: A rumor spreads of a Grogoch spotted near the area.
Adventurers need a component from a Grogoch to complete their quest.
creatures.description: A hairy, haystack-like earth sprite that tends root gardens and guides travelers through safe tunnels in exchange for secrets.
creatures.heritage: This native root-garden earth sprite predates the Great Binding. Rooted in Thalren + Skaldic folklore, the myth of Grogoch originally served as a way for the community to rationalize the forces described in local tales: "Derived from the Skaldic Grogoch, a helpful yet reclusive hedge-spirit, and the Thalren Erdm�nnlein, the industrious little men of the earth, this creature is a master of the soil.". This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It cultivates edible roots, repairs burrows, directs travelers, and trades access for secrets or useful seed

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Grogoch rather than creates it: a native root-garden earth sprite that maintains subterranean food systems and safe routes; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native root-garden earth sprite that maintains subterranean food systems and safe routes.
loreCanon.function: It cultivates edible roots, repairs burrows, directs travelers, and trades access for secrets or useful seed.
loreCanon.values: Soil health, food continuity, secrecy, and the stability of underground paths.
loreCanon.folklore: Hairy haystack form, secret tunnels, and helpful guidance are true. The creature is not created by a story.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The cold made root agriculture crucial; First Cracks supplied warm soil pockets that Grogochs defend from logging and settlement expansion.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native and valuable ally against invasive root corruption. Individual Grogochs can make bad bargains without turning the kind into Wyrdspawn.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether Grogochs are a family-bearing people with names or a network of seasonal garden stewards.

folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Grogoch/Grogochan (Celtic/Irish & Manx folklore):** A hairy, half-human hedge-spirit covered in matted hair, that lives in burrows and helps farmers with harvesting in exchange for milk and solitude.; **Erdmännlein (Germanic folklore):** "Little Earth-Men"  -  subterranean dwarves who tend root-gardens underground and can be glimpsed only at dawn when their tiny spadefuls of earth appear at the surface.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Root-Tender:** Grogochs cultivate vast underground gardens of edible ironwood-roots and frost-tubers, pruning the root-networks of the forest to maximize harvest. Their gardens are the primary food source for many Fog-Peat villages. **The Fog-Herder:** They dig elaborate tunnel-networks beneath the fog-layer, creating safe underground passages between settlements. Thalren who know the Grogoch-tunnels can travel the Reach without risking memory-loss  -  but the Grogoch demand a secret in payment for each passage used.

creatures.name: Cailleach
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Cailleach
creatures.origin: A manifestation of winter's severity and judgment, this entity is born from the Thalren winter goddess Perchta and the Skaldic winter hag Cailleach. In the Frostwood, some folk wrongly credit her with weaving the mist, though the Fog Compact is its true source, enforcing the strict social contracts of House Thalreth.
creatures.nature: This twelve-foot-tall crone presents a shifting appearance: she seems a regal woman in a gown of frost-crystals and ironwood-silk to the diligent, but appears as a skeletal horror in peat-moss rags to the lazy. She carries an ironwood distaff to spin emotion-colored memory yarn, and her face features one piercing blue eye and one hollow, fog-filled socket, with a mouth that freezes the air when she smiles.
creatures.habitat: She wanders the highest, coldest ridges of the Frostwood during winter, descending into the valleys when the fog is thickest.
creatures.combat: 390 HP. Fog-Spinning (passive: generates memory-fog in a 60-ft radius; creatures inside must DC 14 SPI each round or lose one minor memory). Judgment-Gaze (special: perceives each creature's diligence; the hardworking see a radiant queen, the slothful see a skeletal horror). Distaff-Strike (melee, reach 15 ft, +6 to hit, 2d8+4 bludgeoning). Straw-Judgment (special: if she deems a household negligent, she fills their bellies with straw � DC 15 CON save or incapacitated for 24 hours with a stomach full of straw; not lethal but deeply disturbing). Vulnerable to fire.
creatures.depth: Cailleachs spin the memory-fog from raw Wyrd-energy to defend the forest, encoding each strand of mist with a dissolved memory. During the deep winter, they visit Greymark homes to inspect family journals, rewarding diligent scribes with spools of memory-yarn that can restore lost thoughts, while stuffing the bellies of the negligent with straw as a stern warning. Scribes often send adventurers to locate her to seek her favor or harvest her shimmering memory-yarn.
hooks: A rumor spreads of a Cailleach spotted near the area.
Adventurers need a component from a Cailleach to complete their quest.
creatures.description: A towering winter crone who spins the memory-fog and judges the diligence of mortal record-keepers.
creatures.heritage: This native winter crone or highland weather person predates the Great Binding. Rooted in Thalren + Skaldic folklore, the myth of Cailleach originally served the Frostwood as a way to rationalize the memory-fog that eats the Reach's histories and names. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: She judges record-keeping, moves winter pressure, and keeps dangerous highland conditions from collapsing into the valleys

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Cailleach's native baseline rather than creates it: a native winter crone or highland weather person. The current claim that she spins fog from raw Wyrd-energy is rejected as a universal origin; any Wyrd change belongs to an individual or branch.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native winter crone or highland weather person. The current claim that she spins fog from raw Wyrd-energy is rejected as a universal origin.
loreCanon.function: She judges record-keeping, moves winter pressure, and keeps dangerous highland conditions from collapsing into the valleys.
loreCanon.values: Seasonal severity, truthful records, and the boundary between mountain cold and valley survival.
loreCanon.folklore: Winter crone, frost gown, journal inspections, and rewards for diligence are useful truth. "Wyrd weaver" is a later contamination or mortal explanation.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding's winter made the Cailleach's role more severe; First Cracks gave her new thermal boundaries to regulate.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native weather authority with possible Wyrd siphoning in one later branch. Do not make all winter crones Wyrdspawn.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether Cailleach is one person, a lineage of seasonal offices, or a title shared by several native beings.

folkloreInspiration.primaryMyth: Perchta/Frau Holda (Germanic winter folklore) & The Cailleach (Celtic winter mythology)
folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Perchta/Frau Holda (Germanic winter folklore):** A dual-natured winter goddess  -  radiant and generous to the hardworking, but appearing as a hideous crone who punishes the lazy by slitting their bellies and stuffing them with straw.; **The Cailleach (Celtic winter mythology):** The divine winter hag of Gaelic tradition who controls the weather, shapes the landscape with her hammer, and rules the months between Samhain and Beltane.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Fog-Spinner:** Cailleachs are the origin of the memory-fog itself  -  they spin raw Wyrd-energy into the protective mist at the request of ancient House Thalreth. Each thread of fog they spin contains a dissolved memory, woven into the fabric of the forest's defense. **The Judgment-Hag:** During the deep winter, they descend into Greymark's villages and inspect every home. Those who have maintained their journals faithfully receive a spool of memory-yarn that can re-weave one lost memory. Those who have neglected their records wake to find their bellies filled with straw  -  a warning, not a death.

creatures.name: Dullahan
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Dullahan
creatures.origin: Rooted in the Florae myth of the Dullahan, the headless harbinger of death, and the Skald legend of the kopflose Reiter who punishes broken oaths, the Dullahan is a relentless executioner. In the setting of Frostwood Reach, it enforces the sanctity of written vows and the preservation of identity.
creatures.nature: This tall, armored figure clad in blackened ironwood-plate rides a horse composed of compressed fog with a skull-like head. The rider is headless, with memory-mist escaping from its raw neck stump, and it carries its severed head,featuring a featureless, polished ironwood mask that reflects the observer's deepest fears,under one arm. A whip crafted from braided journal-cords hangs at its belt.
creatures.habitat: It haunts the ancient, fog-drowned crossroads and trade routes of the Frostwood at midnight.
creatures.combat: 380 HP. Fear-Mirror (passive: its ironwood mask-face reflects the viewer's deepest fear; DC 14 SPI or frightened for 3 rounds). Name-Call (special: speaks one name into the fog; that person's defining memory begins dissolving within 24 hours). Spine-Whip (melee, reach 15 ft, +6 to hit, 2d6+4 slashing + DC 14 AGI or pulled 10 ft toward the rider). Fog-Mount (passive: its horse is made of fog; immune to physical damage, takes double radiant). Vulnerable to radiant.
creatures.depth: The Dullahan rides to crossroads to whisper a traveler's name, causing their defining memory to dissolve within a day, and actively hunts those who break written oaths recorded in Greymark's ledgers. It is particularly drawn to maskless Mimir, collecting their abandoned identities to fuel its own hollow existence. Local authorities post massive rewards for adventurers who can destroy the rider or retrieve its mirror-like ironwood mask.
hooks: A rumor spreads of a Dullahan spotted near the area.
Adventurers need a component from a Dullahan to complete their quest.
creatures.description: A headless armored rider on a fog-steed that dissolves the identities of named targets and hunts oath-breakers.
creatures.heritage: This native headless death rider tied to named roads predates the Great Binding. Rooted in Thalren + Skaldic folklore, the myth of Dullahan originally served as a way for the community to rationalize the forces described in local tales: "Rooted in the Skaldic myth of the Dullahan, the headless harbinger of death, and the Thalren legend of the kopflose Reiter who punishes broken oaths, the Dullahan is a relentless executioner.". This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It enforces route and oath boundaries, warns a named target, and decides whether a broken agreement merits erasure or pursuit

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Dullahan rather than creates it: a native headless death rider tied to named roads, written oaths, and the dissolution of a person's public identity; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native headless death rider tied to named roads, written oaths, and the dissolution of a person's public identity.
loreCanon.function: It enforces route and oath boundaries, warns a named target, and decides whether a broken agreement merits erasure or pursuit.
loreCanon.values: Names, oaths, and the right of a road to be traveled under honest terms.
loreCanon.folklore: Headless armor, fog horse, name whisper, and memory dissolution are real signs. The death-harbinger story is incomplete but useful.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: Written house contracts and cold roads expanded its jurisdiction; First Cracks made warm trade routes valuable and crowded.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native death office. Wyrd can create a false Dullahan that erases names indiscriminately, but the native rider is not Wyrdspawn.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Define what counts as a valid name and whether a person can escape erasure by publicly repairing the oath.

folkloreInspiration.primaryMyth: Dullahan (Celtic/Irish folklore) & Der kopflose Reiter (Germanic folklore)
folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Dullahan (Celtic/Irish folklore):** A headless horseman who carries his own glowing head, using a human spine as a whip. He rides a black horse and stops to call the name of the person about to die.; **Der kopflose Reiter (Germanic folklore):** The headless rider of German ghost-stories who haunts crossroads at midnight, hunting those who have broken oaths.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Name-Caller:** At the fog-drowned crossroads of the Frostwood, the Dullahan stops its ride and speaks a single name into the mist. That individual's most important memory  -  the one that defines their identity  -  begins to dissolve within 24 hours. **The Oath-Hunter:** It tracks those who have broken written vows recorded in Greymark's ledgers, drawn to the resonance of broken contractual memory. Mimir who have lost their masks are its primary prey  -  it collects abandoned identities the way a magpie collects shinies.

creatures.name: Cusith
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Cu-Sith
creatures.origin: Combining the spectral Florae Cu Sith, whose barks signal doom, and the Skald Schr,ttel, a clever forest predator, the Cusith is a terror of the twilight hours. It tracks its prey through the mist, feeding not on physical flesh but on the raw emotions of its victims.
creatures.nature: This massive hound stands shoulder-high to a mounted rider, its impossibly thin frame covered in dark green fur composed of living ironwood moss, with its rib-cage clearly visible. Its paws leave no trace on the forest floor, and a green glow leaks from its claws and teeth, while its long tail ends in a bioluminescent moss tuft. Its narrow muzzle unhinges to reveal backward-curving green bones for teeth, and its eyes are solid, pupilless emerald wells.
creatures.habitat: It hunts in packs throughout the deep, fog-veiled valleys and dark woods of the Frostwood.
creatures.combat: 220 HP. Three-Bark-Hunt (3 rounds of escalating barks: Round 1, DC 13 SPI or frozen 1 round; Round 2, DC 14 SPI or forget current location; Round 3, target walks willingly into deepest fog � no save, DC 15 SPI to resist at the threshold). Fear-Drain (passive: feeds on the memory of fear; targets within 30 ft who have been frightened lose the emotional memory of fear permanently, becoming eerily calm). Moss-Touch (melee, +5 to hit, 2d6+3 cold damage). Green-Phosphor (passive: emits green bioluminescence, illuminating 20 ft). Vulnerable to fire.
creatures.depth: The Cusith hunts at dusk, using three distinct barks: the first paralyzes a traveler, the second erases their location memory, and the third compels them to walk into the fog's heart. Rather than killing, the hound feeds on the memory of fear, leaving its prey dazed but completely devoid of terror, which allows Florae rangers to track the packs by locating these unnaturally fearless survivors. Adventurers are often sent to hunt these beasts to harvest their glowing moss or save lost travelers.
hooks: A rumor spreads of a Cu-Sith spotted near the area.
Adventurers need a component from a Cu-Sith to complete their quest.
creatures.description: A massive green-furred hound that hunts in the fog, using its barks to paralyze prey and feed on their fear.
creatures.heritage: This native large hound predates the Great Binding. Rooted in Thalren + Skaldic folklore, the myth of Cu-Sith originally served as a way for the community to rationalize the forces described in local tales: "Combining the spectral Skaldic Cu Sith, whose barks signal doom, and the Thalren Schr�ttel, a clever forest predator, the Cu-Sith is a terror of the twilight hours.". This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It culls sick animals, herds lost travelers away from sinkholes, and attacks when a person repeatedly ignores warnings

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Cusith rather than creates it: a native large hound that hunts fog-edge prey and uses layered barks as territorial communication; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native large hound that hunts fog-edge prey and uses layered barks as territorial communication.
loreCanon.function: It culls sick animals, herds lost travelers away from sinkholes, and attacks when a person repeatedly ignores warnings.
loreCanon.values: Pack, den, and safe movement through the fog; its three barks are social signals before they are weapons.
loreCanon.folklore: Green fur, doom barks, and fear feeding are local observations. The hound does not need to be made by fear.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: Cold narrowed prey routes; warm clearings became pack boundaries and human settlement edges.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native beast. A Wyrd-stalked Cusith may overhunt, but the species remains native.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Define the three-bark vocabulary and whether any bark can communicate a safe route to humans.

folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Cu Sith (Celtic fairy-hound):** A spectral green hound of the fairy realm whose three barks warn of death  -  the third bark is never heard by the victim.; **Schrättel (Germanic wolf-spirit):** A predatory forest-ghoul that hunts in pairs, driving game  -  and unwary travelers  -  toward ambush points by howling in falsetto.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Three-Bark Hunt:** Cusith hunt in the fog at dusk. The first bark causes a traveler to freeze with instinctive terror; the second causes them to forget where they are; the third  -  which the victim never consciously hears  -  causes them to walk willingly into the fog's deepest heart. **The Memory-Hound:** They do not eat flesh. They feed on the memory of fear itself, draining the emotional imprint of terror from their prey and leaving behind an eerily calm, hollowed victim who cannot remember feeling afraid. Florae rangers track Cusith packs by finding eerily fearless, lost travelers.

creatures.name: Pixie
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Pixie
creatures.origin: A blend of the Florae Pixie, which leads travelers astray or assists them for small offerings, and the Skald Irrlicht, the deceptive Will-o'-the-Wisp of the peat-bogs, this glowing sprite is a constant companion of the fog. It represents both hope and deception, shifting its behavior on a whim.
creatures.nature: This hand-sized sprite is made of semi-transparent condensed fog-light and shaped like a tiny humanoid with delicate moth-wings. It pulses with a warm honey-colored glow and leaves a trail of phosphorescent spores that hang in the air, changing color from gold to blue or red depending on its mood. Its tiny, mouthless face is dominated by large, solid eyes of warm light through which it communicates.
creatures.habitat: It hovers over the damp marshes, peat-bogs, and low-lying paths of the Frostwood where the mist is thickest.
creatures.combat: 75 HP. Spore-Trail (passive: leaves a colored trail � gold = guides to safety, blue = leads in circles, red = leads to danger; player rolls DC 12 INT to determine color before following). Spore-Burst (AoE 5 ft, DC 12 CON or blinded 1 round). Glow-Pulse (1 AP: doubles light output, illuminating 40 ft). Vulnerable to cold.
creatures.depth: Pixies guide lost travelers through the fog, leaving gold trails that lead to safety, blue trails that run in circles, or red trails that plunge into bogs or over cliffs. They reproduce by seeding spores into the memory-fog, where they grow by absorbing dissolved emotional memories, occasionally creating dense lantern-fogs that travelers can navigate if they understand the colors. Adventurers often seek them to collect their glow-spores for light-sources or mapping reagents.
hooks: A rumor spreads of a Pixie spotted near the area.
Adventurers need a component from a Pixie to complete their quest.
creatures.description: A hand-sized light sprite with moth wings, leading travelers through the fog with shifting colored paths.
creatures.heritage: This native small light-fey predates the Great Binding. Spun from the mystery of marsh gas and will-o'-the-wisps, the Pixie was a folklore explanation for why travelers lost their way in the deep fog. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It guides, misguides, marks safe water, and seeds new lights or spores in a fog ecosystem

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Pixie rather than creates it: a native small light-fey of the bogs and paths. The current `undead` type is likely a taxonomy mismatch unless a death-light variant is intended; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native small light-fey of the bogs and paths. The current `undead` type is likely a taxonomy mismatch unless a death-light variant is intended.
loreCanon.function: It guides, misguides, marks safe water, and seeds new lights or spores in a fog ecosystem.
loreCanon.values: Choice, curiosity, and a route's hidden danger; it enjoys the agency of deciding what color trail to leave.
loreCanon.folklore: Colored trails and offerings are reliable, while the claim that it reproduces only through Wyrd memory spores needs correction.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: Darkness made its light ecologically valuable; First Cracks created warm routes where its spores or eggs could survive.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native light-fey, potentially vulnerable to Wyrd imitation. The undead data type is `DATA-REVIEW` material even though the status remains native review.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether Pixies are fey, elemental light, or death-light spirits and align the JSON `type` later.

folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Piskie/Pixie (Celtic Cornish folklore):** Mischievous little people who lead travelers astray with dancing lights, but can be benevolent to those who leave them offerings.; **Irrlicht/Will-o'-the-Wisp (Germanic folklore):** Ghostly lights that hover over bogs and marshes, luring the curious into mires from which they never return.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Path-Lighter:** Pixies are drawn to lost travelers and will hover ahead, leading the way through the fog. When helpful (gold trail), they guide toward safety. When mischievous (blue trail), they lead travelers in circles. When malicious (red trail), they guide directly into mires or off cliffs. **The Fog-Bloom:** They reproduce by seeding their spores into the memory-fog itself, where the spores germinate into new Pixies after absorbing enough dissolved emotional memory. A fog-bank dense with Pixies is called a "lantern-fog" and is considered navigable  -  if the traveler can tell gold from blue.

creatures.name: Waldschrat
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Waldschrat
creatures.origin: The Waldschrat represents a merger of the Skald Waldschrat, a hairy riddle-loving forest spirit, and the Florae Far Darrig, the red-capped prankster. In the Frostwood, it is a playful yet dangerous manifestation of the forest's tangled history, testing the wit and courage of travelers.
creatures.nature: This three-foot-tall, wiry creature is formed of twisted ironwood-roots and bark, its body dominated by a bright crimson peaked cap of peat-moss. Its highly flexible limbs bend in impossible directions, and it carries a gnarled root-staff that rattles, releasing tiny red sparks when it is pleased. Its leathery, wrinkled face features a wide, lipless grin and mismatched red and green eyes that look in separate directions.
creatures.habitat: It makes its home along the narrow, overgrown paths and dense thickets of the ironwood forests.
creatures.combat: 45 HP. Red-Cap-Spark (ranged, +4 to hit, 1d4 fire). Root-Rattle (AoE 10 ft, DC 12 CON or deafened 1 round). Impossible-Flexibility (immune to grapple and restrain). Fear-Feed (passive: gains +2 to all rolls for each frightened creature within 30 ft). Vulnerable to cold.
creatures.depth: Waldschrats block pathways and demand that travelers solve riddles based on forgotten history, which require pure intuition to answer since the memories themselves have vanished. They also entertain themselves by playing frightening pranks, mimicking the voices of lost scribes, and feeding on the adrenaline of terrified travelers to power their glowing caps. Scribes and rangers frequently seek them out to solve historical mysteries or hire adventurers to drive them away from trade routes.
hooks: A rumor spreads of a Waldschrat spotted near the area.
Adventurers need a component from a Waldschrat to complete their quest.
creatures.description: A wiry wood sprite with a crimson moss cap that blocks forest paths with historical riddles and feeds on fear.
creatures.heritage: This native ironwood-root riddle spirit predates the Great Binding. Rooted in Thalren + Skaldic folklore, the myth of Waldschrat originally served as a way for the community to rationalize the forces described in local tales: "The Waldschrat represents a merger of the Thalren Waldschrat, a hairy riddle-loving forest spirit, and the Skaldic Far Darrig, the red-capped prankster.". This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It blocks unsafe routes, preserves historical memory through questions, and tests whether travelers can live with uncertainty

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Waldschrat rather than creates it: a native ironwood-root riddle spirit, a path guardian whose body is grown from local plant matter; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native ironwood-root riddle spirit, a path guardian whose body is grown from local plant matter.
loreCanon.function: It blocks unsafe routes, preserves historical memory through questions, and tests whether travelers can live with uncertainty.
loreCanon.values: Path memory, old trees, and the right of history to remain difficult rather than simplified.
loreCanon.folklore: Red cap, riddles, and playful obstruction are true. The fear it causes is a side effect of its duties.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding buried paths and made old routes unreliable; warm clearings brought more travelers into its jurisdiction.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native. A Wyrd riddle-horror might counterfeit its questions, but the Waldschrat is not Wyrdspawn.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether its riddles preserve facts, relationships, or emotional truths that the fog has erased.

folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Waldschrat (Germanic forest-spirit):** A wild, hairy wood-spirit that challenges travelers to riddle-contests and devours those who answer incorrectly.; **Far Darrig (Celtic/Irish folklore):** The "Red Man"  -  a prankster-fairy who wears a red cap and delights in terrifying travelers, though he rarely causes true harm.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Riddle-Keeper:** Waldschrats block fog-paths and refuse passage until the traveler answers a riddle constructed from the region's lost history. The riddles are impossible to answer through knowledge  -  they can only be solved by intuition, because the answers are memories that no longer exist. **The Fear-Prankster:** When not riddling, they delight in terror: appearing behind travelers and shouting nonsense-words, mimicking the voices of journal-scribes calling for help, or rattling their staffs to simulate approaching predators. They feed on the adrenaline of fear, which they metabolize into the red phosphorescence that powers their caps.

creatures.name: Gambrel
creatures.illustrationCaption: A spindly, long-limbed Gambrel emerging from the mist near an empty carriage
creatures.origin: The Gambrel is born from the emotional fallout of broken vows and failed compacts in the Frostwood Reach. In a region where written deeds and contracts are the only things preventing total loss of identity, a broken oath is a serious spiritual crime. The Wyrd corruption feeds on this hidden guilt, molding it into a physical stalker.
creatures.nature: It appears as a spindly, long-limbed creature that stands over eight feet tall, with joints that bend in unnatural directions. Its skin is like grey, rotting leather, and it has no face other than a wide, lipless mouth that smells of cold copper. It moves with a silent, jerky gait, and its speed is directly proportional to its prey's desperation to escape their promises.
creatures.habitat: Gambrels haunt the foggy trails and forest paths of the Frostwood Reach, especially near border gates and ruined keeps where broken agreements were made.
creatures.combat: 240 HP. Guilt-Sense (passive: senses target's guilt; speed scales based on target's desperation). Broken Contract (melee, 2d8+3 slashing, reach 10 ft; +2d6 psychic if the target has ever broken a promise). Mist-Vanish (can teleport 30 ft into mist as a reaction). Vulnerable to ember.
creatures.depth: It cannot be outrun by standard horses or clockwork vehicles, as it shifts through space using the target's guilt as a spatial tether. Slaying a Gambrel requires facing it directly, as running only increases its strength and speed.
hooks: A merchant broke a trade oath with a Florae hunter, and now a Gambrel is stalking his family's carriage.
The players are contracted to slay a Gambrel that has locked down a local trade crossing.
creatures.heritage: Derived from the folklore of early settlers regarding the spiritual weight of covenants, literalized by Wyrd anomaly into a relentless hunter of debtors.
creatures.description: A spindly, long-limbed Wyrd-horror that hunts down those who have broken oaths or carry hidden guilt.

loreClassification.agency: It selects a guilty target, follows shame as a spatial tether, and escalates when the target tries to forget rather than repair the harm

creatures.loreNote: Folklore translates Gambrel's Collector/judge and scout/listener function rather than creates it: this ancient cosmic Wyrdkin persists through Fog roads, failed compacts, broken gate stones, and records whose oath language has been erased and is not assumed to be Keth-Amar's offspring.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: An ancient cosmic route-stalker that senses broken relational bonds and uses Frostwood oath guilt as its local hunting language; direct Keth-spawn remains possible but is not the leading answer.
loreCanon.function: It selects a guilty target, follows shame as a spatial tether, and escalates when the target tries to forget rather than repair the harm.
loreCanon.values: The persistence of a broken promise and the territory of its hunt; its apparent morality is predatory compulsion, not Keth-Amar's moral law.
loreCanon.folklore: Oath hunter, impossible pursuit, and guilt-speed are local translation and tactical warning. The underlying native contract culture existed before the Wyrd arrived.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: House oaths and First Cracks supplied the social signal it can now sense; warmth routes make targets and broken bargains more concentrated.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Ancient Cosmic Wyrdkin proposed; a sterile direct Keth-spawn version remains an open alternative.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Confirm ancient migratory species versus Keth-directed offspring and define whether a repaired oath dissolves a Gambrel, transfers its target, or only makes it vulnerable.
loreCanon.cosmicProvenance: Working hypothesis: a Between predator or collector that detects promises, boundaries, and social fractures across inhabited worlds. It may migrate along a predator wake without serving that predator.
loreCanon.wyrdFunction: Collector/judge and scout/listener; it locates damaged trust that can reveal hidden houses or weaken cooperation.
loreCanon.anchor: Fog roads, failed compacts, broken gate stones, and records whose oath language has been erased.
loreCanon.kethRelationship: Keth-Amar can direct it toward a strategic target or use its pursuit to fracture a house, but no direct parentage is established.
loreCanon.independence: It remains active and self-directed after Keth-Amar's retreat, following its own hunt rules and potentially bargaining over a repaired oath.
loreCanon.countermeasure: Repair the obligation, expose the true terms, break the guilt tether, and deny the creature a route through redundant witnesses and honest records.

creatures.name: The Revel
creatures.illustrationCaption: A glowing, phantom celebration in a forest clearing, composed of hollow wooden puppets
creatures.origin: Before the sun died, the Revel was a seasonal celebration of the Seelie court. When the Wyrd seeped into the forest, it trapped the echoes of this celebration, turning the dancers into mindless puppets and the music into a lethal sensory trap.
creatures.nature: The Revel appears as a collection of wood-carved, mask-wearing puppets that dance in a circle around a cold bonfire. The air smells of sweet wine and damp earth, and their music is a compelling, beautiful song that echoes through the trees.
creatures.habitat: Deep ironwood groves and clearing ruins of the Frostwood Reach, especially during moonlit nights.
creatures.combat: 310 HP. Endless Dance (aura, 30 ft: DC 14 SPI or forced to dance, losing 1 AP per turn). Joyous Cacophony (ranged, 2d6 psychic, targets up to 3 enemies). Fey-Step (teleports 40 ft as a free action once per turn). Vulnerable to necrotic.
creatures.depth: Those who enter the circle are caught in the melody and join the dance until their lungs collapse from exhaustion. The puppets themselves are hollow, filled with writhing black thorns that lash out when damaged.
hooks: A group of young archer-initiates disappeared after following music into the woods; they have been dancing for three days.
A Florae clan needs a magical lute that was captured by the Revel's lead puppet.
creatures.heritage: Formed from Seelie festival memories, twisted by Wyrd corruption into a predatory trap.
creatures.description: A phantom court of wooden puppets that forces travelers into an endless, exhausting dance.

loreClassification.agency: It traps travelers in an exhausting dance, preserves a corrupted rite, and expands its circle by converting witnesses into participants

creatures.loreNote: Folklore translates The Revel's Parasite/sower and mimic/interpreter function rather than creates it: this ancient cosmic Wyrdkin persists through Cold bonfire, moonlit clearing, old Seelie song, carved masks, and the boundary of the dance circle and is not assumed to be Keth-Amar's offspring.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A possible ancient cosmic ritual parasite or movement-symbiote occupying a pre-existing Seelie Accord celebration, or a direct Keth-spawn echo generated around that rite.
loreCanon.function: It traps travelers in an exhausting dance, preserves a corrupted rite, and expands its circle by converting witnesses into participants.
loreCanon.values: The shape of celebration without consent, repetition, and the cold bonfire at the center of the Wyrd circle.
loreCanon.folklore: Wooden masks, seasonal dance, music before sight, and the rule not to enter the circle are local camouflage and survival instruction. The original Accord was native and separate.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding disrupted seasonal light and social gatherings; First Cracks created warm clearings that became attractive stages and energy sources for the arriving Wyrd form.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Ancient Cosmic Wyrdkin versus direct Keth-spawn review; do not classify native fae celebrations or the Seelie Accord as Wyrd.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether any native fae can reclaim the celebration, or whether the cosmic organism must be removed as an independent invasive ecology.
loreCanon.cosmicProvenance: Working hypothesis: a Between organism that synchronizes bodies, sound, and group motion as feeding or communication. It may have recognized the Accord's seasonal pattern as a usable local interface.
loreCanon.wyrdFunction: Parasite/sower and mimic/interpreter; it translates a cosmic synchronization behavior into a familiar fae festival and recruits bodies.
loreCanon.anchor: Cold bonfire, moonlit clearing, old Seelie song, carved masks, and the boundary of the dance circle.
loreCanon.kethRelationship: Keth-Amar may have used the ceremony as camouflage or directed the infestation toward the Florae's hidden groves; direct generation is unresolved.
loreCanon.independence: The court can continue dancing without a visible command and may contain factions of puppets that remember the old celebration differently.
loreCanon.countermeasure: Break the rhythm, restore consent, separate native music from the Wyrd pattern, and extinguish or cleanse the anchor without destroying the native clearing.

creatures.name: Skerry
creatures.illustrationCaption: A Skerry clinging to a frozen dock piling, its eyes gleaming with the reflection of stolen gold
creatures.origin: The Skerry is a creature born from the greed of the sea and the cold of the Nordhalla fjords. Before the failing of the warmth, when the Skaldic Kings ruled the frozen north, the water dwarves were the guardians of sunken treasure, spirits who ensured that the wealth of the sea was distributed according to the will of the spirits. When the Great Binding fell, the Skerries were twisted into creatures of insatiable greed, their natural love of beauty and craftsmanship turned into an obsession with hoarding salvaged metal and gold. The sailors of Nordhalla have learned to respect the Skerries, leaving copper coins at the water's edge as a tax for safe passage, but they also fear them, for a Skerry cheated of its due will sink a ship as easily as it will repair one.
creatures.nature: A stout, broad water-sprite with waterlogged blue-grey skin that looks like wet oak. It wears a coat of salvaged sailcloth and copper sheeting, its seams stitched with kelp-fiber. Its webbed fingers end in chisel-like claws of copper, and its eyes are the color of deep water, always scanning for the glint of metal. The Skerry is highly skilled in shipbuilding, able to listen to the stresses in a ship's hull and identify the exact point of weakness. It demands silver or gold for its repairs, and if cheated, it will actively sabotage the vessel, loosening rivets and rotting timber from the inside.
creatures.habitat: The Skerry inhabits the frozen bays, ice-locked docks, and sunken shipwrecks of Nordhalla, particularly in the Sunken Fjord where the wreck of the ancient fleet lies beneath the ice. It is most active during the spring thaw, when the ice breaks and the wrecks are exposed, and during the winter storms, when ships are most likely to need repairs. The Skerries have a complex social structure based on hoard size, and the Skerry with the largest hoard is considered the king of the local waters.
creatures.combat: 265 HP. Rivet Hammer (melee, 2d8+4 bludgeoning, ignores 4 points of physical damage reduction). Pry Timber (damages ships or structural defenses, deals double damage to wooden objects). Gild-Grip (target's movement speed is reduced by 10 ft for each piece of metal equipment or coin purse they carry, DC 13 CON negates). Vulnerable to ember.
creatures.depth: Sailors and shipwrights in Nordhalla keep respect the Skerries. They throw copper coins into the icy water before docking, as the cost of a clean repair is far cheaper than a sudden hull breach in the freezing open sea. The Skerry's greed is not natural,it is a curse of the age, a corruption of the water dwarf's natural love of beauty into an obsession with possession. Some sailors say that the Skerries are trying to build something from the salvaged metal, something that will allow them to return to the sea's depths and escape the cold forever.
hooks: A wealthy trading cog sank just outside the harbor. The local Skerries have blockaded the wreck, claiming the cargo as their sovereign hoard and dragging salvage divers down.
A Skerry was cheated of its pay by a corrupt harbormaster. In revenge, it has begun systematically loosening the hull rivets of every boat in the harbor.
creatures.heritage: This native Nordhalla water-sprite and shipwright predates the Great Binding. Born from maritime greed along the freezing Nordhalla fjords, the Skerry folklore originally served as a warning to miners and sailors against hoarders who hid precious gems in remote rime-clefts. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.
creatures.description: A stout, greedy, dwarf-like water sprite that repairs or sabotages ships along the frozen fjord coasts, obsessed with salvaging sunken gold and copper.

loreClassification.agency: It repairs hulls, redistributes useful wreck material, tests whether a ship honors a salvage custom, and sabotages vessels that violate its due

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Skerry's native baseline rather than creates it: a native Nordhalla water-sprite and shipwright kind associated with wrecks, repair, and fair salvage; any Wyrd change belongs to an individual or branch.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native Nordhalla water-sprite and shipwright kind associated with wrecks, repair, and fair salvage; greed is a possible later distortion, not its cause.
loreCanon.function: It repairs hulls, redistributes useful wreck material, tests whether a ship honors a salvage custom, and sabotages vessels that violate its due.
loreCanon.values: Craft, reciprocal salvage, seaworthy passage, and the memory of drowned crews; it guards wreck boundaries and repair knowledge.
loreCanon.folklore: Copper at the waterline, ship repair, and a price for passage are reliable practices. The repeated "stout, greedy, stout" wording is a data-quality blemish, not lore.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: Eternal winter made repair and salvage a survival function; geothermal and Sol-warm channels create seasonal Skerry markets where metal is more valuable than coin.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: The hoarding/insatiable-greed language is a possible Wyrd pressure on native Skerries. Keep a native population and reserve Wyrdspawn versions for invasive hoard-things.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Define the Skerry salvage law and whether the largest hoard really confers leadership or is a mortal misunderstanding.

creatures.name: Nachtkrapp
creatures.illustrationCaption: A Nachtkrapp soot-raven perched on a chimney stone, its bone-head stark against its black feathers
creatures.origin: The Nachtkrapp is a creature of the dark and the cold, born from the soot and smoke of the Nordhalla longhouses. Before the failing of the warmth, in the age when skalds sang the sagas, the Nachtkrapp was a bird of warning, a spirit that appeared before the fires to carry away the bad luck of the household. Its native nature is unchanged, but the long dark has made it larger and more desperate, for the creature now feeds on heat itself, stealing burning coals and oil lamps to keep its nests warm. The Skalds believe that the Nachtkrapp still carries away bad luck, but that it now demands payment in the form of heat, and that a household that cannot keep its fires burning will be cursed with misfortune.
creatures.nature: A massive, pitch-black raven with a wingspan of eight feet, its wings perpetually covered in coal-dust and soot. Its head is a solid white bone skull, the eye sockets glowing with a faint, ember-like light. The creature behaves like a magpie, but instead of shiny metal, it steals burning coals, oil lamps, and warm ash. It is a domestic pest in northern keeps, but it is also a creature of habit, and it will return to the same chimney night after night, building its nest in the warm soot until the chimney is blocked and the longhouse fills with smoke.
creatures.habitat: The Nachtkrapp nests in the high chimney stacks, volcanic vents, and longhouse roof peaks of Nordhalla, particularly in the capital city of Skaldheim where the longhouses burn day and night. It is most active during the winter, when the fires are burning the brightest and the heat is most needed, and during the volcanic eruptions that occasionally shake the northern peaks. The Nachtkrapp's nest is a massive structure of soot and cinders, warm enough to hatch eggs even in the deepest winter.
creatures.combat: 220 HP. Ash Cloud (vents a cloud of hot soot from its wings, 15-ft radius, DC 13 CON save or blinded and coughing for 1 round). Coal Snatch (melee, attempts to steal a light source or burning item, DC 13 AGI to prevent). Wing Slash (2d6+3 physical damage). Vulnerable to rime.
creatures.depth: A domestic pest in northern keeps. While they steal precious fuel, Skalds believe they carry away domestic bad luck with the soot they scavenge, and leave small trays of tallow outside to pacify them. The Nachtkrapp's skull-head is a mystery to scholars,some say it is the skull of the first Nachtkrapp, worn by every generation as a reminder of the creature's origin. Others say that the skull is a mask, and that beneath it, the Nachtkrapp is a creature of pure fire, its true form too bright for mortal eyes to see.
hooks: A Nachtkrapp has stolen a sacred hearth-coal containing the family line's runic fire. Retrieve the coal before the nest burns down or the fire goes cold.
A giant flock of Nachtkrapps has gathered over the keep's main chimney, blocking the smoke and causing the longhouse to fill with suffocating draft-smoke.
creatures.heritage: This native soot-raven and hearth-warning beast predates the Great Binding. Spun from the soot and smoke of longhouse hearths, the Nachtkrapp was a child-discipline myth told by parents to keep children from playing near drafty chimneys and fires at night. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.
creatures.description: A massive, pitch-black soot-raven with a bone-head that steals fire coals and oil lamps to warm its high chimneys nests.

loreClassification.agency: It carries away ash, nests in warm chimneys, removes failed fuel, and opportunistically steals heat when its brood cannot survive the cold

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Nachtkrapp's native baseline rather than creates it: a native soot-raven and hearth-warning beast that has nested around northern settlements since before the Star-Fall; any Wyrd change belongs to an individual or branch.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native soot-raven and hearth-warning beast that has nested around northern settlements since before the Great Binding.
loreCanon.function: It carries away ash, nests in warm chimneys, removes failed fuel, and opportunistically steals heat when its brood cannot survive the cold.
loreCanon.values: Nest warmth, household continuity, and warning signs; it is protective of a chimney it has adopted but not morally benevolent.
loreCanon.folklore: Bad-luck removal, soot offerings, and coal theft are true observations. The skull may be a species trait, a ritual mask, or a dead elder's relic; it is not evidence of Wyrd origin.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding's darkness made a heat-feeding niche essential. First Cracks and later vents created new nesting corridors and made the bird a visible competitor for scarce fuel.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: A native kind whose desperation may be increased by Wyrd-cold or Shard resonance. Do not classify every heat thief as Wyrdspawn.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether the skull is biological, inherited, or carried, and whether Nachtkrapp family groups deliberately warn households before chimney fires.

creatures.name: Glacier Gremlin
creatures.illustrationCaption: A small Glacier Gremlin licking a frozen runic stone near the crevasses
creatures.origin: The Glacier Gremlin is a creature of the ice and the runes, born from the intersection of highland legends and the cold magic of Nordhalla. Before the failing of the warmth, when rune-singers bound the stones, the ice was alive with spirits, small creatures that absorbed the magic of the runic stones and used it to sustain themselves. Their native spirit is unchanged, but the long dark has made them more desperate, for the runic stones are now few and the competition for their mana is fierce. The Glacier Gremlins are the scavengers of the ice, small creatures that lick the frozen stones to feed on the last traces of magic. The Skalds consider them pests, but they also know that the gremlins are drawn to the most powerful runes, and that their presence is a sign of ancient magic.
creatures.nature: A small, hunched gremlin about a foot tall, with skin made of cracked, translucent blue ice that shows the faint glow of the mana it has absorbed. It is blind and mouthless, using a long, icy tongue to lick the cold runic stones and absorb their power. The creature's body is constantly cold, and it leaves a trail of frost wherever it goes. They are harmless individually, but they are highly annoying, freezing boots to the ice and jamming sled runners with their cold touch. When threatened, they emit a high-pitched whistle that can shatter ice crystals.
creatures.habitat: The Glacier Gremlin inhabits the glacial cols, runic ruins, and ice sheets of Nordhalla, particularly in the Rune-Cleft Glacier where the ancient rune-singers carved their spells into the ice. It is drawn to high concentrations of runic magic, and it is most active during the dark winter months, when the aurora borealis charges the runic stones with additional power. The gremlins are territorial, and fights between rival bands over the best stones are common.
creatures.combat: 45 HP. Frost Lick (melee tongue attack, DC 12 CON save or target's movement speed is halved for 2 rounds as ice creeps up their leg). Runic Absorb (drains 10 mana from a target on a successful hit). Vulnerable to ember (shatters instantly if it takes 10+ ember damage in one hit).
creatures.depth: They are simple elemental pests that are drawn to high concentrations of runic magic. Hunters clear them out of sled paths using torches, but the Skald scholars study them, believing that their icy tongues hold the secret to preserving the runic stones from the decay of time. The Glacier Gremlin's blindness is a blessing, for the runic stones are often too bright for mortal eyes to look upon, and the creature's ice-skin is a natural shield against the stones' radiation.
hooks: A Glacier Gremlin has frozen itself to a crucial runic lever in the mines. Melting it requires heat, but too much heat will detonate the gas pocket nearby.
Skald scholars want three gremlins captured alive; their icy tongues can be used to preserve fragile scrolls without freezing them.
creatures.heritage: This native ice-and-mineral scavenger predates the Great Binding. Created by Nordhalla miners to explain why iron-drills cracked and alchemical pipes froze, the Glacier Gremlin was a scapegoat myth for industrial failures in the extreme cold. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.
creatures.description: A tiny, blind glacier gremlin with cracked blue-ice skin that licks frozen runic stones to feed on mana.

loreClassification.agency: It licks exposed runes and warm mineral seams, clears unstable residue, competes in bands, and signals where ancient energy is concentrated

loreCanon.folklore: Tiny blue pests near powerful stones are true. The claim that they consume mortal magic is a later vocabulary error because Mythrill had no mortal magic before the Great Binding.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: Celestial magic entering house territories made more feedable residue available after Year 0; First Cracks exposed new warm-cold gradients and intensified competition around vents.

creatures.name: Nokk Stallion
creatures.illustrationCaption: A ghostly Nokk Stallion formed of river-mist and cold water, its eyes like pale lanterns
creatures.origin: The Nokk Stallion is a creature of the water and the mist, born from the ancient Skaldic legends of the brook-horse, the water spirit that lures the unwary to their doom. In Nordhalla, where the rivers are cold and the waterfalls are tall, the Nokk Stallions are the guardians of the waterways, spirits that protect the rivers from pollution and overfishing. The long dark has twisted their protective nature into something predatory, and they now lure travelers into the water not to save the river, but to feed their own hunger for the warmth of living bodies. The Nordhalla fishermen know the signs of a Nokk's presence,a mist that rises from the water even on a clear day, and the sound of hooves on stone where no horse should be.
creatures.nature: A ghostly stallion composed entirely of swirling grey river-mist, cold water droplets, and floating river-kelp. Its eyes glow like pale swamp lanterns, and its hooves make no sound on the stones, though they leave a trail of frost wherever they touch. The creature stands near deep pools and waterfalls, offering rides to travelers with a gentle whinny and a bow of its head. When a rider mounts, the Nokk's body becomes solid and cold, and it carries the victim into the deepest part of the water, where it dissolves back into mist, leaving the rider to drown.
creatures.habitat: The Nokk Stallion haunts the deep rivers, cold waterfalls, and misty lakes of Nordhalla, particularly in the Veilwater Falls where the river drops three hundred feet into a pool that is said to be bottomless. It is most active during the early morning, when the mist is thickest and the water is coldest, and during the autumn rains, when the rivers are swollen and the currents are strong. The Nokk is territorial, and each stretch of river is guarded by a single stallion that will fight to the death to protect its domain.
creatures.combat: 160 HP. Water Dash (moves up to 50 ft for 1 AP, leaving a freezing trail). Mist Lure (DC 13 SPI save or target is charmed and compelled to move toward the Nokk). Drown (melee, +5 to hit, DC 13 AGI save or grappled and pulled under the water). Vulnerable to ember.
creatures.depth: Territorial and deceptive spirits. While dangerous, they can be pacified by playing a stringed instrument or offering a clean silver coin to the water. The Nokk's mist-body is a mystery to scholars,some say it is the spirit of a horse that drowned in the river, others that it is a manifestation of the water itself, given form by the river's own spirit. The silver coin is said to remind the Nokk of the sun, which it has not seen since it was bound to the water.
hooks: A local skald went missing near the waterfall; his silver harp was found on the shore, where a Nokk has been spotted.
A merchant cog refuses to cross the river because a Nokk Stallion is standing in the shallows, blocking the ferry path.
creatures.heritage: This native river and waterfall guardian predates the Great Binding. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.
creatures.description: A ghostly stallion formed of river-mist and cold water that lures travelers onto its back in Nordhalla.

loreClassification.agency: It regulates pollution, overfishing, and dangerous crossings, and chooses whether to ferry, warn, mislead, or drown a traveler

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Nokk Stallion's native baseline rather than creates it: a native river and waterfall guardian, shaped like a horse because it mediates travel and water access; any Wyrd change belongs to an individual or branch.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native river and waterfall guardian, shaped like a horse because it mediates travel and water access; it was not born from Wyrd fear.
loreCanon.function: It regulates pollution, overfishing, and dangerous crossings, and chooses whether to ferry, warn, mislead, or drown a traveler.
loreCanon.values: Clean current, spawning grounds, and the dignity of the water; it guards a defined stretch of river rather than all travelers.
loreCanon.folklore: Hoof sounds, sudden mist, silver offerings, and a dangerous ride are real signs. The claim that Wyrd made the guardian predatory should be limited to a later branch.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: Glacial darkness and frozen channels reduced the guardian's territory; Sol-warm seepage creates rare open water where Nokk families can breed and where humans compete for passage.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native baseline, with Wyrd pressure potentially turning one Nokk into a hunger-driven invasive predator. Use `HYBRID-REVIEW` until that individual/branch is separated.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether Nokk territories are hereditary river offices, solitary claims, or a network of water agreements.

creatures.name: Huldra
creatures.illustrationCaption: A Huldra forest nymph standing in a sunbeam, her cow tail hidden in the grass
creatures.origin: The Huldra is a creature of the deep forest and the lonely heart, born from the fjord-folk legends of the forest spirits that seduce the unwary. In Nordhalla, where the pine forests are ancient and the winters are long, the Huldras are the spirits of the trees that have been cut, the forest's grief given form. The long dark has twisted their protective nature into something predatory, and they now lure woodcutters and miners into the forest not to protect them, but to bind them to the forest's will. The Nordhalla woodcutters know the signs of a Huldra's presence,a beautiful song on the wind, and the smell of pine needles where no pine trees grow.
creatures.nature: A beautiful woodland spirit that appears as a young maiden with long golden hair and eyes the color of forest pools. She hides a cow's tail beneath her skirts, and her back is completely hollow like a rotting tree, a feature that is only visible when she turns away. She moves with the grace of a dancer, and her voice is a soft, melodic song that can charm the most hardened warrior. She is drawn to lonely woodcutters and miners, offering them comfort and warmth in the cold forest, but her embrace is a trap, and those who succumb to her are never seen again.
creatures.habitat: The Huldra inhabits the ancient pine groves, forest springs, and mining paths of Nordhalla, particularly in the Deepwood where the trees have stood since the pre-Binding era. She is most active during the winter, when the cold drives travelers to seek warmth, and during the spring, when the sap runs and the forest is most alive. The Huldra's territory is marked by small shrines of stones and pine cones, offerings left by those who have escaped her embrace.
creatures.combat: 160 HP. Seductive Song (DC 13 SPI save or target is charmed and must move toward the Huldra). Wood-Slam (+5 to hit, 2d8+3 physical, she possesses supernatural strength). Tree Meld (can teleport up to 40 ft between pine trees). Vulnerable to cold iron.
creatures.depth: Reclusive spirits of the deep forest. They are peaceful if their trees are respected but will curse woodcutters who cut ancient sacred groves. The Huldra's hollow back is a symbol of her nature,she is empty inside, a vessel for the forest's grief, and those who fill her with their love are consumed by it. Some scholars believe that the Huldra was once a mortal woman who loved the forest so deeply that she became one with it, and that her curse is to seek that love forever, never finding it.
hooks: A miner has gone missing; his boots were found near a deep forest pool where a beautiful maiden has been seen singing.
A Huldra has cursed a village logging camp, causing their axes to break on the wood, because they cut a sacred rowan tree.
creatures.heritage: This native Nordhalla forest nymph and tree-person predates the Great Binding. Born from fjord-folk legends of forest nymphs, the Huldra was a warning myth told to young men to prevent them from wandering alone into deep woods in search of romance. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.
creatures.description: A seductive forest nymph with a cow's tail and a hollow tree-back that charms woodcutters in Nordhalla.

loreClassification.agency: It protects old trees, misdirects destructive woodcutters, and can grant or deny access to springs and mining paths

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Huldra's native baseline rather than creates it: a native Nordhalla forest nymph and tree-person, with the hollow back as an honest body trait or a sign of an old ecological wound; any Wyrd change belongs to an individual or branch.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native Nordhalla forest nymph and tree-person, with the hollow back as an honest body trait or a sign of an old ecological wound.
loreCanon.function: It protects old trees, misdirects destructive woodcutters, and can grant or deny access to springs and mining paths.
loreCanon.values: Old growth, spring water, and the dignity of the forest against extraction.
loreCanon.folklore: The cow tail, hollow back, charm, and punishment of careless woodcutters are useful truth. Seduction is not the whole person.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: Eternal winter tightened forest range; First Cracks made warm pine pockets valuable refuge and intensified conflict with miners.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native baseline. A Wyrd-possessed Huldra may lure victims for invasive purposes, but the native nymph is not Wyrdspawn.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether Huldra recognize a common forest law with the Vila, Mossmaiden, and other native plant spirits.

creatures.name: Fossegrim-Ice
creatures.illustrationCaption: A Fossegrim frozen beneath a blue waterfall, playing a fiddle of ram skull
creatures.origin: The Fossegrim-Ice traces its origins to the legendary water-spirits of Skaldic folklore, who lured mortals to waterfalls with the promise of sublime musical mastery, mingled with the highland legends of the Barbegazi, the snowshoe-footed ice-dwarves who whistle warnings of cascading snow. In the frozen expanse of Nordhalla, this spirit has become a creature of absolute winter, bound to the silent cascades where the elements hold sway.
creatures.nature: Entombed within the blue ice of frozen waterfalls, the creature appears as a slender, translucent silhouette holding a fiddle carved from the bleached, frozen skull of a ram. Its body is composed of layered, cross-sectioned sheets of ice that transition through every shade of azure, terminating in massive, snowshoe-like feet that grant it the uncanny ability to glide over the thinnest drifts without fracturing the crust. Its face is a masterpiece of inhuman symmetry, carved with flawless precision, featuring eyes of solid, pale blue ice that look through frozen barriers as if they were nothing more than clear glass.
creatures.habitat: These glacial spirits reside amidst the frozen waterfalls, icy ravines, and sub-zero crevices that scar the stark terrain of Nordhalla.
