creatures.heritage: This native sentient freshwater pool or subterranean water person predates the Great Binding. Spun from pre-Binding water myths of the sacred freshwater abyss, the Abzu represented the hope of finding clean, life-giving water under the desert. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It cools vaults, stores knowledge in water, and trades secrets for a measured blood contribution

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Abzu rather than creates it: a native sentient freshwater pool or subterranean water person, older than the volcanic house settlements; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native sentient freshwater pool or subterranean water person, older than the volcanic house settlements.
loreCanon.function: It cools vaults, stores knowledge in water, and trades secrets for a measured blood contribution.
loreCanon.values: Water purity, memory held in the pool, and the thermal balance of the underground system.
loreCanon.folklore: Circular glowing pool, ancient glyphs, blood exchange, and cooling function are reliable. The pool is not a Wyrd portal by default.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: Sol's burial made cooling water necessary; First Cracks expanded the vault system and made Abzu a strategic resource.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native water intelligence and possible purifier. Wyrd can contaminate a tributary or falsify a secret, but Abzu is independent.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide how Abzu stores knowledge and what happens when a secret is refused or a blood price is unpaid.

folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Abzu/Apsu (Mesopotamian mythology):** The primordial underground freshwater ocean  -  the source of all rivers and wells, and the dwelling-place of Enki, the god of wisdom and magic.; **Nun/Nu (Egyptian mythology):** The primordial waters  -  the cosmic ocean from which all creation emerged, personified as a deity. Nun was the deep, dark, waters-of-creation that surrounded and underlay the ordered world.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Wisdom-Well:** The Abzu is a sentient repository of pre-Dimming knowledge. Those who drink from the pool receive a single piece of forgotten wisdom  -  but the pool takes something in exchange: a drop of the drinker's blood, which becomes part of its eternal archive. **The Volcanic-Coolant:** Its waters cool the geothermal systems beneath the Harath-Vault. Without the Abzu's underground spring feeding the cooling-channels, the forges would overheat and the Sol's Breath would boil dry. Korr engineers maintain the channel-system with reverent precision  -  the Abzu is not a pet or a servant; it is a partner in survival.

creatures.name: Kur-Pit
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Kur
creatures.origin: The Kur-Pit is a breach in reality where the realms of the dead bleed into the land of the living. Its name is derived from Kur, the Fexric underworld of no return, and Duat, the Solvarn labyrinthine world of trials through which the sun traveled each night. It represents a physical manifestation of the dark, subterranean afterlife.
creatures.nature: The Kur-Pit is a perfectly circular, ten-foot-wide abyss that opens in the earth, its smooth walls covered in spiraling hieroglyphic and cuneiform warnings that glow with a dull red light. A constant, echoing murmur of dead voices rises from its depths, and the air above it shimmers with both heat and cold. It has no physical face, but from certain angles, the opening resembles a screaming mouth, with the glyphs acting as lips and the bottomless black as its throat.
creatures.habitat: These abyssal openings appear without warning in the volcanic fields and historical battlefields of Sundale and the Emberspire terrain.
creatures.combat: 760 HP. Underworld-Mouth (passive: a perfectly circular pit, 10 ft across, that opens without warning; those who fall in are trapped in the labyrinth between Kur and Duat � a solo-adventure zone that may take centuries to navigate). Glyph-Warn (passive: walls are covered in spiraling hieroglyphic and cuneiform warnings that glow faintly red; DC 16 INT to read fast enough to stop a companion from falling in). Murmur-of-Dead (passive: continuous sound of countless voices in dead languages; DC 14 SPI or shaken, -2 to all checks within 50 ft). Sun-Path-Reveal (special: during Emberspire's annual vent-calm, Sol's Breath's light momentarily illuminates the nearest Kur, revealing a path that may connect to Sol's prison � no one who has entered has returned). Abyssal-Grip (passive: creatures within 10 ft of the edge feel a gravitational pull toward the pit; DC 13 AGI each round or slide 5 ft closer). Vulnerable to none (it is a geography feature; only sealing it with a major ritual can close it).
creatures.depth: Kur-Pits open spontaneously near areas of great tragedy, trapping the souls of those who fall within the labyrinth of the underworld. During the annual vent-calm of Emberspire, the light of Sol's Breath shines down the pit, momentarily revealing the path to the buried sun-spirit Sol. Scholars believe that navigating this dangerous path may be the only way to free Sol, but since no one has ever returned from a Kur-Pit, the theory remains untested, and adventurers are warned to avoid these areas unless they possess the courage to brave the land of no return.
hooks: A rumor spreads of a Kur spotted near the area.
Adventurers need a component from a Kur to complete their quest.
creatures.description: A circular, bottomless fissure covered in glowing red runes that murmurs with the voices of the dead. It is a portal to the underworld, briefly illuminated by Sol's Breath during the annual vent-calm.
creatures.heritage: This native or Old World liminal geological feature connecting death and living land predates the Great Binding. Rooted in Sumerian underworld legends, the Kur represented the spatial dread of the abyss where the dead wander and the earth swallows the living. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It opens near tragedy, traps or releases souls, and follows a cyclical vent or battlefield pattern

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Kur-Pit rather than creates it: a native or Old World liminal geological feature connecting death and living land; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native or Old World liminal geological feature connecting death and living land; the record is a phenomenon rather than a normal creature.
loreCanon.function: It opens near tragedy, traps or releases souls, and follows a cyclical vent or battlefield pattern.
loreCanon.values: The boundary of the dead, the integrity of its route, and the exchange required to cross.
loreCanon.folklore: Circular runes, dead voices, underworld passage, and brief Solbrand illumination are useful signs. A rumor does not open the pit.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding made the underworld boundary politically important; First Cracks and Breach heat created more openings near tragedy.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native liminal feature unless a particular pit is a Wyrd breach. Do not call every Kur-Pit Wyrdspawn.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether Kur-Pit belongs in `creatures.json` or should become a location/hazard record in a later data model.

folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Kur / Kurnugia (Sumerian mythology):** The Sumerian underworld  -  a dark, dreary realm beneath the mountains where all souls went after death regardless of their deeds. Ruled by Ereshkigal, it was the "Land of No Return."; **Duat (Egyptian mythology):** The Egyptian underworld  -  a dangerous, labyrinthine realm through which the sun-god Ra traveled each night, battling the forces of chaos. Souls navigated its trials to reach the Field of Reeds.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Underworld-Mouth:** Kur-Pits are breach-points where the geography of the underworld bleeds into the surface. They open spontaneously near sites of mass death  -  old battlefields, volcanic eruption zones. Those who fall in are not merely killed; their souls are trapped in the labyrinth between Kur and Duat, navigating trials that may take centuries. **The Sun-Path:** During Emberspire's annual vent-calm, the Sol's Breath's light momentarily illuminates the nearest Kur-Pit, revealing a glimpse of the path beneath. Korr scholars believe this path connects to the buried sun-god Sol  -  and that navigating it may be the only way to reach Sol's prison directly. No one who has entered a Kur-Pit has ever returned to confirm.

creatures.name: Mushussu
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Mu�?u��u
creatures.origin: The Mushussu is a rare and gentle juvenile beast representing new life and creation. Its mythic origins combine the Mushhushshu, the Fexric dragon-serpent of the Ishtar Gate, and Heket, the Solvarn frog-goddess of fertility and childbirth who breathed life into newborns. In the harsh, barren landscape of Sundale, it is welcomed as a harbinger of hope and fertility.
creatures.nature: The size of a large dog, the Mushussu has the long, scaled body of a serpent-dragon, with pale, translucent white scales that reveal its veins beneath. It walks on stubby lion paws in the front and small, underdeveloped eagle talons in the back, and its tail ends in a soft, wobbly stinger. Its face is a cute, rounded version of the adult Sirrush, with a small nub for a horn and large, curious gold eyes, and it communicates through soft, frog-like croaks.
creatures.habitat: These young dragons are found in the warm nesting grounds, rocky crevices, and agricultural borders of Sundale and Emberspire.
creatures.combat: 380 HP. Imprint-Follow (special: imprints on the first kind creature it encounters, following them like a duckling; the bond encourages the adult Sirrush to guard the child's village). Life-Breath (passive: breath accelerates plant growth; a garden visited by a Mu�?u��u produces double yields � invaluable in ash-choked soil). Croak-Communicate (communicates via frog-like croaks; endearing but limited). Nub-Horn-Bonk (melee, +3 to hit, 1d4 bludgeoning � it is a baby). Scamper (can move through difficult terrain without penalty). Vulnerable to cold.
creatures.depth: Unlike their territorial parents, Mushussuren are highly affectionate and will imprint on the first friendly creature they meet, following them like a pet. They possess a magical breath that doubles the agricultural yield of any soil they visit, making them incredibly valuable to Waste-Solari farmers who leave bowls of milk to attract them. The Hollow-Solari tolerate their presence near settlements because the bond helps ensure that adult Sirrush will guard the villages, and adventurers are often hired to protect these juveniles or locate lost ones in the wild.
hooks: A rumor spreads of a Mu�?u��u spotted near the area.
Adventurers need a component from a Mu�?u��u to complete their quest.
creatures.description: A dog-sized, pale serpent-dragon with lion paws and eagle talons. It imprints on friendly creatures, using its fertility-blessed breath to double crop yields in ash-choked soil.
creatures.heritage: This native juvenile serpent-dragon and fertility beast predates the Great Binding. Derived from Babylonian dragon myths of sacred companions, the Mu�?u��u represented the hope of new creation and the taming of wild elements. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It imprints on a companion, fertilizes ash soil, and moves between warm nesting sites and cultivated margins

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Mushussu rather than creates it: a native juvenile serpent-dragon and fertility beast whose gentle life cycle predates the Star-Fall; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native juvenile serpent-dragon and fertility beast whose gentle life cycle predates the Great Binding.
loreCanon.function: It imprints on a companion, fertilizes ash soil, and moves between warm nesting sites and cultivated margins.
loreCanon.values: Nest warmth, a chosen bond, and the continuity of plant life in ash soil.
loreCanon.folklore: Dog-sized body, serpent-dragon shape, fertility breath, and affectionate imprinting are true. It is not a lesser Wyrd dragon.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: Sol warmth provides its habitat; First Cracks expanded fertile borders and made Mushussu valuable to desperate farmers.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native and not Wyrdspawn. A Wyrd-tainted breath or forced imprint is an individual crisis.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether its fertility breath improves soil, pollinates plants, or carries a microscopic native symbiosis.

folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Mushhushshu (Mesopotamian mythology):** The "Furious Snake" of Babylon  -  the dragon on the Ishtar Gate, with a serpent's body, lion's forelegs, eagle's hind-legs, and a scorpion's stinger. (Note: the bestiary's "Sirrush" is the adult form; this is a juvenile variant.); **Heket (Egyptian mythology):** The frog-goddess of fertility and childbirth  -  a deity who breathed life into newborns and assisted in the moment of creation. Frogs were sacred symbols of life's beginning.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Sacred-Juvenile:** Mushussuren are the juvenile form of the Sirrush  -  and they are far more approachable than the fierce adults. They imprint on the first kind creature they encounter, following them like ducklings. Solari children sometimes raise orphaned Mushussuren as pets  -  a practice the Korr tolerate because the bond encourages the adult Sirrush to guard the child's village. **The Life-Breath:** Drawing from Heket's fertility-domain, the breath of a Mushussu can accelerate plant growth. A garden visited by a Mushussu produces double yields. In Sundale's ash-choked soil, this ability is priceless  -  Thrask farmers leave offering-bowls of milk near Sirrush nesting-grounds to encourage juvenile visits.

creatures.name: The Cinder
creatures.illustrationCaption: A burning humanoid child-shape radiating intense heat, walking among scorched basalt
creatures.origin: The Cinder is born from Solvarn folklore regarding children who wandered into the volcanic rifts. The Wyrd anomaly twisted these stories, creating entities of pure ash and fire that seek out and burn liars.
creatures.nature: It appears as a small child-shape composed of white-hot charcoal and glowing ash. It speaks in a crackling whisper that sounds like dry wood catching fire, and it leaves footprints of molten basalt behind it.
creatures.habitat: Volcanic craters, sulfur mines, and basalt canyons of Sundale.
creatures.combat: 290 HP. Liar's Mark (passive: detects spoken lies. Attacks against liars deal +2d8 ember damage). Ash Aura (passive aura, 10 ft: block sight and deals 1d6 fire/turn). Volcanic Flash (melee, +7 to hit, 2d8 ember + DC 13 CON or Blinded 1 round). Vulnerable to cold.
creatures.depth: The Cinder is intensely hostile to anyone who has lied in its presence, ignoring all other targets to consume the liar. It is a symbol of the harsh, unforgiving justice of the Ash-Dwellers.
hooks: A Neth contract-scribe is being hunted by a Cinder after he lied about a debt-agreement's interest rates.
The Dawn Vigil seeks to capture a Cinder to use its flame to test the purity of their penitents.
creatures.heritage: Derived from tales of children lost to volcanic rifts, twisted by Sol's entombed distress.
creatures.description: A small, burning humanoid child-shape of ash and fire that seeks out and consumes liars.

loreClassification.agency: It selects liars, consumes their heat and bodies, and ignores other targets while the lie remains unacknowledged

creatures.loreNote: Folklore translates The Cinder's local form rather than creates it: this direct Keth-spawn depends on Volcanic craters, sulfur mines, ash piles, and the heat gradient around Emberspire's breach conduit, and it can persist briefly in ash after Keth-Amar retreats, but likely requires an active vent or Wyrd residue to reproduce.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A direct Keth-spawn: a Wyrd body generated after arrival and shaped by the Ash-Dweller fear of children lost in volcanic rifts. It is not a native fire child or an ancient species claim yet.
loreCanon.function: It selects liars, consumes their heat and bodies, and ignores other targets while the lie remains unacknowledged.
loreCanon.values: The invasive rule that spoken falsehood must burn; its child shape is a lure, not a childhood.
loreCanon.folklore: Child silhouette, white-hot ash, crackling whisper, and liar targeting are the local blueprint and tactical tell after Wyrd arrival.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding made Solari truth and fire sacred; First Cracks created volcanic sites where Keth's later Wyrd output could attach to that vulnerability.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Direct Keth-spawn / Wyrdspawn proposed.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Confirm direct Keth generation and define whether truth must be confessed by the target, witnessed by a community, or simply understood by the Cinder.
loreCanon.cosmicProvenance: No stable ancient cosmic provenance is established; this may be a local larval form produced from Keth's ash-bearing Wyrd medium. An older cosmic fire scavenger model remains possible.
loreCanon.wyrdFunction: Collector/judge and siege organism; it breaks trust in Solari witnesses and makes every confession a possible attack surface.
loreCanon.anchor: Volcanic craters, sulfur mines, ash piles, and the heat gradient around Emberspire's breach conduit.
loreCanon.kethRelationship: Directly generated or actively refreshed by Keth-Amar's Wyrd; it is a strategic local tool rather than an independent cosmic fauna population.
loreCanon.independence: It can persist briefly in ash after Keth-Amar retreats, but likely requires an active vent or Wyrd residue to reproduce.
loreCanon.countermeasure: Expose the lie without feeding panic, sever the ash anchor, cool and cleanse the site, and redirect the entity to a controlled truth ritual.

It is not a native fire child or an ancient species claim yet. It selects liars, consumes their heat and bodies, and ignores other targets while the lie remains unacknowledged.

creatures.name: Ash-Woven Oracle
creatures.illustrationCaption: A faceless figure of compacted ash and volcanic dust, floating above a sulfur vent
creatures.origin: The Ash-Woven Oracle is a manifestation of the collective fear of the final dimming. It is composed of compacted volcanic ash, held together by Wyrd currents, and speaks in fragmented prophecies.
creatures.nature: A faceless, floating humanoid drape of ash and soot. It carries a bowl of liquid lava, and its body constantly sheds ash clouds that make breathing difficult for nearby creatures.
creatures.habitat: Sulfur vents, active craters, and badland shrines of Sundale.
creatures.combat: 220 HP. Soot Prophecy (ranged, 3d6 psychic, DC 14 SPI or target misses next attack). Ash Cloud (creates a 15-ft cloud of ash that blocks line of sight and chokes enemies). Oracle's Sight (immune to blind, sees future movements, granting +3 to Evasion). Vulnerable to cold.
creatures.depth: Its prophecies are always dark, warning of the complete freeze of the caldera and the starvation of humanity. The soot it sheds is toxic and can cause lung-scarring in miners.
hooks: An Ash-Woven Oracle has nested near the main mining shaft, choking the workers and prophesying a cave-in.
The players need to consult the Oracle to find the location of a hidden geothermal pipe junction.
creatures.heritage: Formed from the soot-blinded shamans who prophesied the death of Sol.
creatures.description: A faceless creature of volcanic ash that speaks dark prophecies and chokes enemies with soot clouds.

loreClassification.agency: It broadcasts dark predictions, chokes excavators, and turns uncertainty into paralysis around vents and shrines

creatures.loreNote: Folklore translates Ash-Woven Oracle's local form rather than creates it: this direct Keth-spawn depends on Sulfur vents, active craters, badland shrines, and ash channels connected to Emberspire, and it can continue speaking without a visible command, but its body depends on ash flow and Wyrd currents.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A likely direct Keth-spawn condensed from Wyrd ash around the collective fear that Emberspire and Sol's warmth will finally dim. An ancient cosmic oracle species is not ruled out.
loreCanon.function: It broadcasts dark predictions, chokes excavators, and turns uncertainty into paralysis around vents and shrines.
loreCanon.values: The narrative of inevitable freeze and the social despair that keeps people from acting.
loreCanon.folklore: Faceless ash drape, lava bowl, toxic soot, and fragmented prophecy are the local translation and tactical tell.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: Sol's Binding and First Cracks created the warmth whose loss people fear; the Oracle uses those scars as a post-arrival anchor.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Direct Keth-spawn / Wyrdspawn proposed, with ancient cosmic oracle provenance unresolved.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Determine whether any prophecy is accurate, self-fulfilling, or only a weaponized pattern of shared fear, and settle ancient fauna versus direct spawn.
loreCanon.cosmicProvenance: Unknown. The current body behaves like a local Wyrd condensation, but it could be a juvenile ash-prophet from the Between using Sundale's volcanic matter.
loreCanon.wyrdFunction: Mimic/interpreter and collector/judge; it translates cosmic pressure into prophecy and harvests the choices made under despair.
loreCanon.anchor: Sulfur vents, active craters, badland shrines, and ash channels connected to Emberspire.
loreCanon.kethRelationship: Likely generated or intentionally directed by Keth-Amar to make Sundale abandon or misuse the Sol/Aex binding; direct command after Blizzard’s End is unknown.
loreCanon.independence: It can continue speaking without a visible command, but its body depends on ash flow and Wyrd currents.
loreCanon.countermeasure: Compare prophecy against verifiable evidence, clean the air, sever the ash current, and stop the community from treating its narrative as inevitable.

creatures.name: Husque
creatures.illustrationCaption: A tear in reality shaped like a humanoid, leaking void energy and pulling objects closer
creatures.origin: The Husque is a mobile rip in spatial reality, a localized leak of Keth-Amar's hunger that has occupied a shell of basalt and mineral slag.
creatures.nature: It appears as a humanoid silhouette made of a shifting, black void that absorbs all light. Basalt plates and copper veins float around its edges, held in place by intense gravitational pulls.
creatures.habitat: Deep sulfur mines, badland gorges, and Monolith excavation sites in Sundale.
creatures.combat: 390 HP. Rift Pull (ranged, +6 to hit, pulls targets 15 ft closer to the Husque). Reality Leak (passive aura, 15 ft: random magical disruptions or 1d8 Wyrd damage). Devouring Breach (melee, +7 to hit, 3d8+6 physical/void damage, heals for half). Vulnerable to radiant.
creatures.depth: It eats the gravity around it, causing pebbles and weapons to float towards its chest. If the Husque is destroyed, it collapses into a harmless heap of basalt, but it leaves a temporary spatial tear.
hooks: A deep mine has been evacuated after a Husque appeared, swallowing ore carts and pulling miners into the shaft.
Dawn Vigil researchers want the core of a collapsed Husque to study gravity containment.
creatures.heritage: Born from miners' dread of tunneling into unstable spatial rifts beneath the Peaks.
creatures.description: A humanoid silhouette of absolute void that distorts gravity and leaks the Sun-Eater's hunger.

loreClassification.agency: It eats local gravity, draws matter toward its chest, and leaves temporary spatial damage after the body collapses

creatures.loreNote: Folklore translates Husque's local form rather than creates it: this direct Keth-spawn depends on Spatial tears, Monolith excavation sites, basalt slag, and the pressure around the Sol/Aex conduit, and it can move between nearby anchors but likely collapses when the breach is sealed and cannot establish a self-sustaining population.

loreCanon.values: Its feeding tear and access to warmth, mass, and spatial stability; agency is emerging predation rather than culture.

loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding and First Cracks supplied the seal geometry and volcanic matter; Aex Shards and excavation sites give the post-Keth body durable anchors.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Direct Keth-spawn / Wyrdspawn proposed.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Confirm whether Husque is a repeatable Keth-spawn organ or a single breach-born entity with no breeding cycle.

loreCanon.anchor: Spatial tears, Monolith excavation sites, basalt slag, and the pressure around the Sol/Aex conduit.

creatures.name: Pelagos
creatures.illustrationCaption: A Pelagos bounding through the icy spray, its bioluminescent whiskers twitching
creatures.origin: The Pelagos is a creature of the sea and the sky, born from the fusion of salt-depth maritime tales and the pre-Binding legends of the Hippocampus. In the Iceheart Sea, where the waters are cold and the reefs are treacherous, the Pelagos are the guardians of the deep, creatures that were created to protect the treasures of the sea from those who would steal them. Their native spirit is unchanged, but the long dark has made them more fierce, for the creature now sees all who enter the water as potential thieves, and it will attack any who disturb the peace of the deep. The coastal fishers of the Iceheart Sea have learned to respect the Pelagos, and they will not fish in the waters where the creatures are known to hunt.
creatures.nature: A sleek hound resembling a greyhound but covered in smooth, rubbery shark skin with deep indigo and sea-foam green countershading. It has webbed paws, a dolphin-like dorsal fin, and a powerful shark tail that propels it through the water with incredible speed. Its chin features soft, glowing sensory whiskers that detect movement under freezing waters, and its eyes emit a soft green bioluminescence that can be seen from a hundred feet away. The Pelagos is intelligent enough to be trained, and it is fiercely loyal to those who earn its trust.
creatures.habitat: The Pelagos inhabits the coastal reefs, ice shelves, and kelp forests of the Iceheart Sea, particularly in the Myrathil Reef where the waters are warmest and the fish are most plentiful. It is most active during the dawn and dusk, when the light is low and the prey is active, and during the spring migration, when the whales pass through the Iceheart Sea and the Pelagos follows them. The creature's den is always near a source of fresh water, for the Pelagos is a creature of both sea and land, and it needs to drink as well as swim.
creatures.combat: 155 HP. Spume Bite (melee, 2d6+4 piercing, plus DC 12 CON save or bleeds for 1d6 physical damage per round for 3 rounds). Bioluminescent Flash (emits a sharp flash of light from its eyes, 30 ft range, DC 13 AGI save or blinded for 1 round). Slipstream (moves 50 ft, ignoring difficult terrain in water). Immune to rime, resistant to physical.
creatures.depth: Highly intelligent and trainable companions. Coastal fishers and Deep-Born divers domesticate them to guide ships through rocky shoals, retrieve dropped anchors, and alert crews to low-frequency underwater vibrations. The Pelagos' bioluminescence is a mystery to scholars, for it is not the cold light of the deep, but the warm light of the surface, and some believe that the creature is a bridge between the two worlds, a creature that belongs to neither and both.
hooks: A pack of feral Pelagos has begun harrying fishing boats near the reefs. The local fishers want them driven off, but a Deep-Born elder claims they are fleeing a far larger predator waking in the trench.
An albino Pelagos, sacred to Olokun, was captured by a Neth merchant for sale. The Myrathil reef-keepers hire the party to break into the merchant's warehouse and rescue it before it is shipped off.
creatures.heritage: This native coastal hound/sea-beast predates the Great Binding. Spun from salt-depth maritime tales and pre-Binding legends of the Hippocampus, the Pelagos pack hunters originally served as warning stories to keep divers from venturing far from the shore. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.
creatures.description: A sleek, hound-like sea hunter with smooth indigo-green shark skin, webbed paws, a shark tail, and glowing whiskers that sense vibrations in freezing currents.

loreClassification.agency: It guides boats, retrieves lost tools, warns of low-frequency danger, and protects reef nurseries from destructive traffic

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native coastal hound/sea-beast lineage that mediates reef travel and underwater vibration; its shape is a local adaptation, not Wyrd assembly.
loreCanon.function: It guides boats, retrieves lost tools, warns of low-frequency danger, and protects reef nurseries from destructive traffic.
loreCanon.values: Pack bonds, reef health, safe passage, and the right of deep-water creatures to remain undisturbed.
loreCanon.folklore: Fishers are right that Pelagos can be trained and that glowing whiskers read vibration. The current Wyrd-fierceness claim should become an individual response to hunting pressure.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: Eternal cold compressed reef life into thermal pockets; Sol warmth from cracks creates breeding refuges and makes Pelagos more valuable to coastal settlements.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native baseline, with possible Wyrd-tainted packs or false Pelagos used to lure divers. Do not make the kind Wyrdspawn.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Establish whether Pelagos are domesticated, mutually bonded, or merely tolerant of trained coastal partners.

creatures.name: Egbere
creatures.illustrationCaption: An Egbere weeping on a coastal rock, its small seaweed-mat head shield catching the spray
creatures.origin: The Egbere is a creature of the sea and the sorrow, born from the salt-depth legends of the small, crying spirits that carry magical mats. In the Iceheart Sea, where the waves are cold and the rocks are sharp, the Egbere are the spirits of the drowned, creatures that were once children who perished in the sea and were transformed by their native element into something that is both pitiful and dangerous. Their native spirit is unchanged, but the long dark has made them more desperate, for the creature now cries not for itself, but for the living, and its tears are a lure that draws the unwary to their doom. The sailors of the Iceheart Sea know the sound of the Egbere's cry, and they will cover their ears when they hear it, for the creature's voice is a siren song that cannot be resisted.
creatures.nature: A small, amphibious humanoid with skin covered in wet scales and seaweed, sitting on coastal rocks or in dark caves, holding a small woven kelp mat on its head. It emits a loud, mournful crying sound that sounds like a lost child, and its eyes are large and black, reflecting the light of the moon. If a sailor attempts to rescue it, the Egbere attempts to steal their iron tools, using a blinding wave of salt water to escape. The creature is not evil, but it is hungry, and it will do whatever it takes to survive.
creatures.habitat: The Egbere inhabits the sea caves, rocky shoals, and reef borders of the Iceheart Sea, particularly in the Weeping Rocks where the waves crash against the shore with a sound like crying. It is most active during the stormy season, when the waves are high and the ships are most likely to be wrecked, and during the full moon, when the light is bright and the creature's eyes are most visible. The Egbere's cave is always near a source of fresh water, for the creature is a creature of both sea and land, and it needs to drink as well as swim.
creatures.combat: 130 HP. Crying Call (AoE, 60 ft range, DC 13 SPI save or target is charmed, compelled to move toward the Egbere). Mat Shield (+4 defense while holding its woven mat). Salt Wave (30-ft cone, DC 13 AGI save or blinded by salt for 1 round). Vulnerable to ember.
creatures.depth: They are greedy beach-scavengers. The woven mat they carry is magically water-resistant; if stolen, it can be sold for a high price to shipwrights. The Egbere's mat is a mystery to scholars, for it is woven from a seaweed that does not exist in any known catalog, and some believe that the creature weaves the mats from its own hair, a process that takes a hundred years and is the creature's only purpose in life.
hooks: A trading boat was lured onto a reef by a crying Egbere, and the crew is now stranded on a rocky islet. Rescue them before the tide rises.
A Myrathil scholar wants the party to steal an Egbere's mat without killing the sprite. The mat holds the secret to weaving water-resistant sails.
creatures.heritage: This native littoral scavenger and drowned-place spirit predates the Great Binding. Rooted in salt-depth legends of crying reef-sprites, the Egbere originally served to explain the mournful, high-pitched whistling of wind through the hollows of coastal rocks, warning travelers against stealing items washed ashore. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.
creatures.description: A small amphibious humanoid that carries a woven kelp mat and cries like a lost child to lure ships onto reefs.

loreClassification.agency: It salvages wreckage, tests whether sailors respect a reef, and uses crying calls to defend a cave or drive intruders away

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Egbere's native baseline rather than creates it: a native littoral scavenger and drowned-place spirit that carries a kelp mat; any Wyrd change belongs to an individual or branch.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native littoral scavenger and drowned-place spirit that carries a kelp mat; the claim that all Egbere were children transformed by Wyrd is rejected as universal canon.
loreCanon.function: It salvages wreckage, tests whether sailors respect a reef, and uses crying calls to defend a cave or drive intruders away.
loreCanon.values: Its mat, cave, drowned kin, and the integrity of a dangerous reef; it values possession because salvage is survival.
loreCanon.folklore: The lost-child cry, amphibious body, and woven water-resistant mat are reliable signs. The drowned-child explanation is one culture's grief story, not the true origin of every Egbere.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding froze shore access and concentrated Egbere around navigable cracks; later warmth opened new reefs while making them vulnerable to salvage and capture.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native baseline with a possible Wyrd-occupied false cry or child-shaped variant. Keep `HYBRID-REVIEW` until the native and invasive forms are named.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether Egbere communities trade mats collectively or whether each mat is an inherited personal territory.

creatures.name: Scylla-Crab
creatures.illustrationCaption: A Scylla standing on an ice floe, its volcanic glass shell glinting in the pale light
creatures.origin: The Scylla-Crab is a creature of the deep and the dark, born from the maritime myths of Scylla and the northern tales of giant crustaceans. In the Iceheart Sea, where the waters are cold and the volcanic vents are hot, the Scylla-Crabs are the guardians of the deep, creatures that have evolved to survive in the most extreme environments. Their native spirit is unchanged, but the long dark has made them more aggressive, for the creature now sees all who enter its territory as a threat, and it will attack any who come near its ice sheet. The fishermen of the Iceheart Sea know the signs of a Scylla-Crab's presence,a field of ice that is too smooth, and the absence of any other life.
creatures.nature: A giant crustacean with a shell made of dark, jagged volcanic glass (obsidian) and frozen sea-spray, its body the size of a small boat. It has massive, asymmetrical claws capable of cutting wooden hulls or crushing ice sheets, and its eyes line the rim of its shell like small, glowing blue beads. The creature moves with a slow, deliberate pace, but it can strike with incredible speed, and its claws are sharp enough to cut through steel. The Scylla-Crab is a creature of instinct, and it will defend its territory to the death.
creatures.habitat: The Scylla-Crab inhabits the ice sheets, glacier walls, and volcanic vents of the Iceheart Sea, particularly in the Obsidian Flats where the volcanic vents are most active and the ice is thickest. It is most active during the winter, when the ice is thickest and the creature's territory is most secure, and during the volcanic eruptions, when the vents are active and the water is warm. The Scylla-Crab's lair is always near a source of heat, for the creature is a creature of both fire and ice, and it needs the warmth to survive.
creatures.combat: 390 HP. Obsidian Claw (+6 to hit, 2d8+5 physical, ignores 3 points of armor). Ice Cutter (+6 to hit, DC 14 AGI save or target's leg is pinned, halving their speed). Volcanic Steam (AoE, vents hot steam from its shell, 15-ft cone, 2d6 ember damage). Vulnerable to storm.
creatures.depth: Highly aggressive, territorial predators. They defend their ice sheets fiercely, striking instantly at any vessel or explorer that draws near. The Scylla-Crab's obsidian shell is a mystery to alchemists, for it is harder than any known material and it does not melt. Some scholars believe that the shell is made of the same material as the volcanic vents, and that the creature is a piece of the earth's fire, brought up to guard the ice.
hooks: A giant Scylla has crawled onto a village's fishing ice sheet, making it impossible for the villagers to harvest fish.
Craftsmen want to harvest the volcanic glass shell of a Scylla to forge shield plates that resist both extreme cold and heat.
creatures.heritage: This native giant crustacean adapted to the Iceheart's collision predates the Great Binding. Spun from pre-Binding maritime myths of Scylla, the multi-headed cliff monster, this giant crustacean originally rationalized why ships collided with submerged rocks in narrow channels. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.
creatures.description: A massive crab with a shell of volcanic glass and frozen sea-spray that guards Iceheart ice floes.

loreClassification.agency: It filters reef water, excavates ice shelves, controls shellfish populations, and defends a breeding floe with immediate aggression

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Scylla-Crab rather than creates it: a native giant crustacean adapted to the Iceheart's collision of volcanic heat and frozen spray; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native giant crustacean adapted to the Iceheart's collision of volcanic heat and frozen spray; Scylla imagery is a later human comparison.
loreCanon.function: It filters reef water, excavates ice shelves, controls shellfish populations, and defends a breeding floe with immediate aggression.
loreCanon.values: Brood, stable ice, vent access, and a shell territory free of large vessels.
loreCanon.folklore: The obsidian shell and sudden attacks near an ice floe are true. The claim that it is a single mythic monster or Wyrd creation is not needed.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The frozen world made vent-fed shelves essential nursery sites; First Cracks and Sol warmth enlarged some shelves while destabilizing others.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native and likely resistant due to its mineral shell. A Wyrd parasite could turn a shell into an invasive harbor hazard, but that is a separate individual story.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether the shell is biologically grown glass, vent-mineral accretion, or a seasonal molt.

creatures.name: Draugr Helmsman
creatures.illustrationCaption: A sea-drenched Draugr Helmsman fused to a rotting ship wheel, seaweed coiling around its skull
creatures.origin: The Draugr Helmsman is a creature of the sea and the dead, born from the Skaldic maritime tales of the undead sailors who guard their sunken ships. Though Skaldic in origin, the Draugr Helmsman has spread to the Iceheart Sea through centuries of Nordhalla shipwrecks, the frozen dead of sunken Skald vessels rising to crew whatever wreckage drifts into warmer currents. In the Iceheart Sea, where the waters are cold and the wrecks are many, the Draugr Helmsmans are the spirits of the drowned, creatures that have been bound to their ships by the force of their own greed. Their native spirit is unchanged, but the long dark has made them more vengeful, for the creature now sees all who approach its wreck as thieves, and it will attack any who try to salvage its cargo. The divers of the Iceheart Sea know the signs of a Draugr's presence,a ship that is too well preserved, and the sound of a helmsman's whistle in the depths.
creatures.nature: A sea-drenched, blue-skinned undead sailor whose hands are fused to the rotting wood of a ship's helm wheel, its body draped in frozen blue kelp, barnacles, and rotting ropes. Its eyes glow with a chilling frost-light, and it speaks in a hollow, wind-swept whistle that can be heard through the water. The creature is bound to its ship, and it cannot move more than a hundred feet from the wreck. It is a creature of tragedy, and its rage is a thing of terrible beauty, for it is the rage of a man who died for his cargo and will not rest until it is safe.
creatures.habitat: The Draugr Helmsman haunts the shipwrecks, frozen bays, and ice floes of the Iceheart Sea, particularly in the Graveyard of the North where the wrecks of countless ships lie beneath the ice. It is most active during the winter, when the ice is thickest and the wrecks are most accessible, and during the storms, when the waves are high and the ships are most likely to sink. The Draugr's presence is a sign that the wreck is still sealed, and that the cargo within is still guarded.
creatures.combat: 200 HP. Rotting Anchor (+5 to hit, 2d8+3 bludgeoning, reach 10 ft). Sea-Salt Curse (DC 13 SPI save or target's lungs fill with salt water, choking and dealing 1d8 damage per round). Frost Bind (ranged, DC 13 CON save or target is frozen in place). Vulnerable to ember.
creatures.depth: Tragic, vengeful spirits bound to their sunken ships. They protect the cargo they died carrying, dragging salvage divers down into the freezing deep. The Draugr's frost-light is a mystery to scholars, for it is not the cold light of the dead, but the warm light of the living, and some believe that the creature is not truly dead, but suspended between life and death, a guardian that will never rest.
hooks: A salvager cog is trapped in a frozen bay because a Draugr Helmsman has anchored their chain to his sunken ship.
A scholar wants the helmsman's runic compass, believed to be able to navigate through the thickest sea fogs.
creatures.heritage: This native death-bound maritime spirit predates the Great Binding. Born from Skaldic maritime tales of undead sailors guarding their wrecks, the Draugr Helmsman was a warning to prevent looting of sunken ships. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.
creatures.description: A sea-drenched undead mariner fused to a rotting ship wheel, guarding sunken wrecks in the Iceheart Sea.

loreClassification.agency: It keeps a wreck's last route, protects or denies salvage, and decides whether a living diver honors the dead crew

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Draugr Helmsman rather than creates it: a native death-bound maritime spirit that remains attached to a ship, crew, or cargo after an uncompleted voyage; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native death-bound maritime spirit that remains attached to a ship, crew, or cargo after an uncompleted voyage; it is not automatically Wyrd undead.
loreCanon.function: It keeps a wreck's last route, protects or denies salvage, and decides whether a living diver honors the dead crew.
loreCanon.values: Crew obligation, cargo promises, burial, and the identity of the vessel it once steered.
loreCanon.folklore: Fused helm, frost-light, vengeful salvage defense, and maritime warnings are likely true. "Wyrd made it vengeful" is a correction target.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding's darkness and frozen routes increased wrecks and created more unresolved voyages; Sol-warm currents can temporarily release or awaken a Helmsman.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native liminal form. Wyrd can occupy a wreck and imitate a Helmsman, but native dead-ship spirits should remain distinct.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Define the rule for release: burial, delivery of cargo, naming the lost, or completion of the original route.

creatures.name: Qalupalik
creatures.illustrationCaption: A scaly Qalupalik emerging from an ice crack, its long claws reaching out
creatures.origin: The Qalupalik is a creature of the ice and the dark, born from the Rime-Born mythology of the humanoid sea creatures that carry away children. In the Iceheart Sea, where the ice is thick and the water is cold, the Qalupaliks are the spirits of the frozen, creatures that have been shaped by their native ecology into something that is both pitiful and terrifying. The long dark did not change their nature, but it did make them more predatory, for the creature now sees all who approach the ice as prey, and it will drag any who come near into the water. The parents of the Iceheart Sea know the signs of a Qalupalik's presence,a humming song on the wind, and the absence of any children.
creatures.nature: An amphibious, scaly humanoid sprite with dark green skin and long, slimy hair that smells of sulfur. It wears a large seal-skin parka with an oversized hood (amautik) on its back, and it hides beneath ice cracks, waiting to grab travelers and drag them down. The creature is stealthy and patient, and it can wait for hours beneath the ice, its only movement the slow rise and fall of its breathing. The Qalupalik is a creature of the dark, and it is most active during the long winter nights, when the ice is thickest and the children are most likely to wander.
creatures.habitat: The Qalupalik inhabits the frozen ocean shores, glacier fissures, and ice wells of the Iceheart Sea, particularly in the Child's End where the ice is thin and the water is deep. It is most active during the winter, when the ice is thickest and the children are most likely to wander, and during the spring thaw, when the ice cracks and the creature can reach through. The Qalupalik's lair is always beneath the ice, in a cave that is warm and dry, and it is said to be a place of terrible beauty, filled with the bones of the creature's prey.
creatures.combat: 155 HP. Amautik Snatch (+5 to hit, DC 13 AGI save or pulled into the Qalupalik's hood and restrained). Ice Dive (can submerge into freezing water for 1 AP, avoiding attacks). Claw Strike (2d6+3 physical). Vulnerable to ember.
creatures.depth: Stealthy, solitary hunters. They use a low, humming song to lure unwary children and travelers close to the ice cracks, dragging them down to live in their sub-glacial caves. The Qalupalik's amautik is a mystery to scholars, for it is made of a seal-skin that does not exist in any known catalog, and some believe that the creature skinned the seals itself, a process that takes a hundred years and is the creature's only purpose in life.
hooks: A child was snatched from the shore ice by a Qalupalik. The party must venture down into the ice caves under the bay to rescue her.
Hunters want to study the insulated seal-skin hood of a Qalupalik, believing it holds a secret to surviving extreme freezing wind.
creatures.heritage: This native Iceheart ice-well hunter or subglacial amphibious person predates the Great Binding. Rooted in highland mythology of humanoid child-snatchers, the Qalupalik was a cautionary tale to keep children from playing near cracking ice-sheets and freezing water edges. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.
creatures.description: An amphibious scaly sea-humanoid that snatch travelers from ice-wells in the Iceheart Sea.

loreClassification.agency: It controls access to thin ice, hunts at cracks, and may collect living prey as food, hostages, or members of a hidden subglacial community

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Qalupalik's native baseline rather than creates it: a native Iceheart ice-well hunter or subglacial amphibious person; any Wyrd change belongs to an individual or branch.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native Iceheart ice-well hunter or subglacial amphibious person; the child-snatcher story records dangerous encounters but does not create it.
loreCanon.function: It controls access to thin ice, hunts at cracks, and may collect living prey as food, hostages, or members of a hidden subglacial community.
loreCanon.values: A safe ice route, a cave, young, and the boundary between surface travelers and subglacial water.
loreCanon.folklore: Humming lures, an amautik-like carrying wrap, and dragging prey under ice are reliable signs. "Spirit of the frozen" is a human category, not a full origin.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding froze open water and forced Qalupalik into narrow wells; Sol-warm currents create contested refuges where they can move closer to shore.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native baseline with potential Wyrd child-lure outbreaks. Keep `HYBRID-REVIEW` until a non-Wyrd social ecology is written.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether Qalupalik are solitary predators or a hidden people with a reason for taking travelers alive.

creatures.name: Mamiri
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Mamiri
creatures.origin: The legend of the Mamiri echoes the ancient myths of the pre-Binding seas, where avian or piscine maidens sang from shores of bone to wreck passing vessels, blended with the salt-depth traditions of Mami Wata. In the freezing expanses of the Iceheart Sea, she manifests as a powerful, seductive water-spirit associated with immense wealth, fertility, and highly dangerous bargains. She demands absolute devotion from those who dare seek her favor, punishing any hint of betrayal with watery graves.
creatures.nature: Standing upon the jagged, frozen reefs, she appears from the waist up as a heartbreakingly beautiful woman with skin the deep indigo of abyssal waters and eyes the warm, horizontal-pupiled green of shallow sea-shallows. Instead of a fish's tail, her lower half dissolves into a churning column of sea-foam and dark kelp, which reaches out like grasping hands toward the shore. She wears a crown of sharp coral and cowrie shells, and around her neck hangs a jangling collar of gold coins harvested from the pockets of drowned sailors. Her long, black hair moves of its own accord, swaying through the spray as she sings with full lips that never cease their deadly, hypnotic melody.
creatures.habitat: These creatures reside in the freezing, iceberg-strewn waters of the Iceheart Sea, where they perch on semi-submerged rocks and jagged reef formations.
creatures.combat: 160 HP. Song-Lure (AoE 120 ft, DC 14 SPI save or overwhelming compulsion to move toward the Siren; ice-sheets amplify the song, extending range). Cowrie-Crown-Bargain (special: offers deals � wealth, safe passage, prime fishing-grounds � in exchange for a personal treasure, secret, or years of life; deals are binding if sealed with a cowrie shell). Kelp-Hair-Grasp (melee, reach 10 ft, +5 to hit, 1d8+3 bludgeoning + DC 13 AGI or grappled). Vulnerable to lightning.
creatures.depth: She sits on freezing reefs and sings. She doesn't want gold; she demands 'warm memories.' To pass her reef safely, a player must let her touch their forehead and draw out one happy memory (e.g., their first kiss, a childhood birthday), which they then forget forever.
hooks: A sailor survived a shipwreck but forgot his wife's name after meeting a Mamiri.
A reef can only be bypassed by giving up a happy memory.
creatures.description: A creature of tragic and terrifying beauty, this sea-spirit lures sailors to their doom with an irresistible song.
creatures.heritage: This native reef and sea-song spirit predates the Great Binding. Derived from pre-Binding Siren myths, the Mamiri originally rationalized the tragic lure of beautiful, auditory hallucinations that led exhausted sailors to wreck their ships on bone-strewn shores. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It controls a reef passage, collects warm memories as food or exchange, and decides which sailors may pass

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Mamiri rather than creates it: a native reef and sea-song spirit whose beauty and voice mediate a dangerous boundary, not a rumor-born siren; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native reef and sea-song spirit whose beauty and voice mediate a dangerous boundary, not a rumor-born siren.
loreCanon.function: It controls a reef passage, collects warm memories as food or exchange, and decides which sailors may pass.
loreCanon.values: Reef territory, song, and the emotional warmth needed to survive a cold sea.
loreCanon.folklore: Reef singing, memory payment, and shipwreck danger are true. It wants more than gold because its ecology is relational.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding froze most open water and made reefs more dangerous; First Cracks created warm channels where Mamiri can gather.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native sea spirit. A Wyrd lure may copy its song, but Mamiri are not Wyrdspawn.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Define whether warm memories sustain the spirit physically, preserve its song, or are simply the accepted price for passage.

folkloreInspiration.primaryMyth: Siren (Greek mythology) & Mami Wata (West African/Yoruba tradition)
folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Siren (Greek mythology):** The bird-women (later fish-women) whose impossibly beautiful singing lured sailors to crash their ships on rocky shores. Homer described them as sitting in meadows of bones.; **Mami Wata (West African/Yoruba tradition):** A powerful water-spirit  -  a beautiful, seductive mermaid-figure associated with wealth, fertility, and dangerous bargains. She demands devotion and punishes betrayal.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Song-Lure:** Her singing carries across the water for miles, amplified by the ice-sheets that act as acoustic mirrors. The song does not charm  -  it creates a powerful, overwhelming desire to move toward the source. Victims walk off decks, lower boats, or dive into freezing water to reach her. **The Bargain-Spirit:** Like Mami Wata, she offers deals: wealth from sunken ships, safe passage through storms, or the location of prime fishing-grounds  -  in exchange for a personal treasure, a secret, or years of the sailor's life. Those who honor the bargain prosper; those who cheat her find their ships mysteriously sinking within the month.

creatures.name: the Maelstrom
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary the Maelstrom
creatures.origin: The the Maelstrom is born of the pre-Binding myth of the primordial whirlpool, which swallowed the seas three times a day to drag ships to the deep, merged with the salt-depth legend of the Dingonek, a scaly, leopard-spotted water-beast. In the Iceheart Sea, she is a colossal, elemental force of destruction, a natural counterpart to other coastal terrors.
creatures.nature: This creature presents as a rotating mass of dark water and fragmented ice forty feet wide, hiding the shifting, massive form of a leopard-spotted serpentine body that is never visible as a whole. Shield-sized spotted scales flash momentarily at the vortex's edge before being dragged back down into the depths. The water within the maw is hot and stinks of sulfur and rotting fish, roaring like thunder as it feeds. At the deepest point of the whirlpool lies a circular, terrifying mouth lined with rotating rings of serrated, spotted scales like a lamprey's throat scaled to architectural proportions.
creatures.habitat: This creature anchors itself in the narrow shipping channels and treacherous straits between the ice-fields of the Iceheart Sea.
creatures.combat: 505 HP. Whirlpool-Vortex (passive: anchors in narrow shipping channels; any vessel within 100 ft is pulled 20 ft closer each round, DC 16 STR or AGI to resist). Swallow-Cycle (special: swallows water and debris, then expels in a geyser � expels cargo of consumed ships as treasure-currents; Deep-Born follow these to salvage). Leopard-Scale-Flash (passive: spotted scales flash at the vortex edge; the pattern disorients, DC 13 SPI or confused 1 round). Lamprey-Throat (melee, +7 to hit, 2d10+5 piercing + DC 15 STR or swallowed; swallowed targets take 4d6 acid per round). Vulnerable to lightning.
creatures.depth: A massive circular maw that swallows entire ships. Its gullet is a treasure trove of shipwrecked gold and ancient weapons. Players can cast a rope into its mouth to fish for loot, but if they pull too hard, they might be dragged in.
hooks: A legendary sword is believed to be sitting inside the gullet of a the Maelstrom.
A vessel was swallowed whole, and survivors might be alive in its air-pocket stomach.
creatures.description: A terrifying vortex of dark water and spotted scales, this living whirlpool devours entire ships in narrow shipping lanes.
creatures.heritage: This native whirlpool organism or sea phenomenon with a living maw and a stable feeding route predates the Great Binding. Rooted in the pre-Binding myth of the primordial whirlpool monster, the the Maelstrom was a to explain lethal, sudden ocean vortexes that swallowed vessels. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It regulates a shipping strait, consumes wrecks, and leaves routes open when currents and prey require it

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Charybdis rather than creates it: a native whirlpool organism or sea phenomenon with a living maw and a stable feeding route; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native whirlpool organism or sea phenomenon with a living maw and a stable feeding route.
loreCanon.function: It regulates a shipping strait, consumes wrecks, and leaves routes open when currents and prey require it.
loreCanon.values: The channel, feeding territory, and current pattern that sustains it.
loreCanon.folklore: Ship-swallowing vortex, spotted scales, and wreck treasure are accurate. Sailors turn a living ecological hazard into a singular myth.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding made currents and ice shelves more rigid; First Cracks shifted its strait and made it a major trade hazard.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native sea predator/phenomenon. Wyrd may infest wreckage inside it, but the vortex is not Wyrdspawn.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether Charybdis has a body that can move or is a fixed living current with a seasonal appetite.

folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Charybdis (Greek mythology):** The monstrous whirlpool that swallowed and expelled water three times a day, creating a vortex so powerful it could drag ships beneath the waves. She was the counterpart to Scylla.; **Dingonek (West African/Congo cryptid):** A walrus-like water-beast with a scaly body, spotted like a leopard, said to inhabit rivers and lakes. It was large enough to capsize canoes and kill crocodiles.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Navigation-Hazard:** Charybdiss anchor themselves in the narrow shipping channels between ice-fields, creating deadly vortexes that activate without warning. The Merryn navigate by memory-charts of known Maw locations, but the creatures migrate slowly  -  a chart that is accurate one season may be lethal the next. **The Swallow-Cycle:** Like the mythological Charybdis, they swallow water and debris, then expel it in enormous geysers. The expelled material includes the cargo of ships they have consumed  -  creating treasure-currents that Deep-Born Myrathil follow to salvage sunken wealth.

creatures.name: Ketos
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Ketos
creatures.origin: The Ketos draws its mythic lineage from the pre-Binding Cetus, the colossal sea-monster sent to ravage the Sunken Cities and slain by ancient heroes, combined with the deep-sea legend of the Grootslang, a mistake of the spirits that possessed the intellect of an elephant and the body of a serpent. In the setting, it exists as a titanic relic of creation that inhabits the darkest trenches.
creatures.nature: Spanning over two hundred feet in length, this leviathan combines the serpentine body of an ancient sea-dragon with the massive, tusked head of an elephant. Overlapping, whale-grey plates cover its immense body, which is underscored by bioluminescent organs pulsing with a deep blue light. Two thirty-foot tusks of yellowed ivory curve from its upper jaw, framing rowboat-sized eyes that are milky with cataracts. Its massive jaw hinges like a serpent's, and its colossal face bears an expression of ancient, bored contemplation.
creatures.habitat: This leviathan dwells in the dark, pressurized depths of the Treakous Oceanic Rift, coiling near the fragments of the Sundered Monolith.
creatures.combat: 700 HP. Trench-Coil (passive: coils around the Sundered Monolith fragment; its movements cause the Monolith's resonance to fluctuate). Elephant-Tusk-Ram (melee, reach 20 ft, +8 to hit, 3d8+6 bludgeoning; ships struck take structural damage equal to half the damage). Bioluminescent-Pulse (passive: slow deep-pulse blue light along its underside; visible from miles in the dark ocean). Swallow-Whole (special: mouth large enough to swallow a small ship; DC 18 STR or vessel and crew are swallowed, taking 5d6 acid per round). God's-Mistake-Intellect (passive: enormous, intelligent brain; it may try to communicate through telepathic dreams rather than fight). Vulnerable to psychic (its own intelligence makes it vulnerable to mental assault � psychic damage ignores 50% of its resistances).
creatures.depth: So massive that its back gathers ice and soil, looking like a small harbor island. It only submerges if it hears a whale's song; bards can play a whale-song on a shell flute to soothe it back to sleep, allowing ships to escape its wake.
hooks: A group of fishers anchored on what they thought was an island, but it began to breathe.
A leviathan is blockading a port, and bards are searching for a whale-song flute.
creatures.description: A primordial sea-monster of colossal scale, this tusked serpent guards the deepest rifts of the ocean floor.
creatures.heritage: This native abyssal leviathan predates the Great Binding. Derived from the pre-Binding Cetus, the colossal sea-monster sent by spirits, the Ketos represented the fear of coastal devastation and massive tsunamis. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It shapes deep-sea pressure, sleeps through surface eras, and chooses whether whale song or ships count as intrusion

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Ketos rather than creates it: a native abyssal leviathan, an old sea lineage that predates the Great Binding and knows the Treakous Rift as a nursery or border; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native abyssal leviathan, an old sea lineage that predates the Great Binding and knows the Treakous Rift as a nursery or border.
loreCanon.function: It shapes deep-sea pressure, sleeps through surface eras, and chooses whether whale song or ships count as intrusion.
loreCanon.values: Rift depth, brood, and the pressure balance of the abyss.
loreCanon.folklore: Island-sized back, tusks, and whale-song sleep are useful observations. It is not a Wyrd dragon or a creation of the Monolith.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding altered surface currents and pushed more ice downward; First Cracks made the rift's heat and resonance more active.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native leviathan. Wyrd may feed on its wounds or the nearby Monolith, but Ketos itself is not Wyrdspawn.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether Ketos recognizes the Monolith as an intruder, a wound, or an unrelated human object.

folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Ketos/Cetus (Greek mythology):** The primordial sea-monster sent by Poseidon to terrorize Troy  -  a serpentine whale-creature of enormous size, slain by Heracles. The constellation Cetus is named for it.; **Grootslang (South African legend):** A massive elephant-serpent hybrid said to inhabit a deep river-cave in South Africa. Legend says the gods made it as a mistake  -  combining the brain of an elephant with the body of a snake  -  and it became so dangerous they had to banish it.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Trench-Dweller:** The Ketos inhabits the Treakous Oceanic Rift  -  the same trench that holds the Sundered Monolith. It is drawn to the Monolith's resonance-frequency, coiling around the fragment in the dark. Deep-Born Myrathil can feel its presence in their teeth alongside the Monolith-hum. **The God's-Mistake:** Like the Grootslang, it is a creature that should not exist  -  a fusion of incompatible designs by an ancient creative force. Its brain is enormous, intelligent, and capable of complex problem-solving. Some Deep-Born believe it has been trying to communicate with the Monolith for centuries, attempting to solve the puzzle of its own existence.

creatures.name: Harpy
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Harpy
creatures.origin: The Harpy traces its folklore roots to the pre-Binding Harpy, the wind-spirit of sacred punishment that stole souls and food, and the Ashanti Asanbosam, a forest-canopy vampire with iron teeth and hooked feet. In the Iceheart Sea, these creatures act as agents of localized tempests and scavengers of the masts.
creatures.nature: Having the wings, talons, and feathered torso of an oil-dark vulture, this creature possesses the gaunt, gray-skinned chest and face of a hag. Its feet are not talons but curved iron hooks that resemble grappling irons, dripping with freezing sea-water. The creature smells strongly of rotting fish, and its waterlogged feathers make its flight noisy and labored. Its hollow-cheeked face is dominated by furious, lightning-colored eyes and a wide mouth filled with filed iron teeth.
creatures.habitat: These creatures nest in the eyes of perpetual cyclones and perch in the sails, rigging, and masts of ships sailing the Iceheart Sea.
creatures.combat: 135 HP. Mast-Snatcher (special: perched in rigging, snatches crew from decks; +6 to hit, 2d6+3 slashing + DC 14 AGI or grappled and lifted 20 ft). Iron-Hook-Feet (passive: feet are curved iron hooks; cannot be dislodged from masts without dealing 20 damage to the Harpy or breaking the mast). Storm-Rider (passive: nests in the eye of perpetual storms; navigates cyclones perfectly; seeing one means a storm exit-corridor exists nearby � Navigation check DC 13 to follow it safely). Feather-Slash (melee, +5 to hit, 1d8+3 slashing). Vulnerable to fire.
creatures.depth: Harpys attack ships by perching in the rigging, dangling upside-down to snatch crew members from the decks with their iron hook-feet. Once they grip a mast, they cannot be dislodged without breaking the wood or killing the creature outright. Sailors fear them as death-omens, yet also use them as navigation aids since they always fly toward the calmest exit-corridors of cyclones. A recent squall has left a merchant fleet stranded, and the crew is hiring mercenaries to clear the harpies from their masts.
hooks: A rumor spreads of a Harpy spotted near the area.
Adventurers need a component from a Harpy to complete their quest.
creatures.description: A storm-riding terror with iron hook-feet and vulture wings, this avian hag snatches sailors from the rigging.
creatures.heritage: This native storm-wing scavenger and cliff predator predates the Great Binding. Spun from pre-Binding Harpy legends of sacred thieves, this wind-spirit originally rationalized sudden, violent squalls that swept away crops, sails, and drying fish. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It hunts exposed sailors, scavenges storm kills, and protects a cyclone nest from ships that approach too closely

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Harpy rather than creates it: a native storm-wing scavenger and cliff predator, with hook feet adapted to rigging and ice; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native storm-wing scavenger and cliff predator, with hook feet adapted to rigging and ice.
loreCanon.function: It hunts exposed sailors, scavenges storm kills, and protects a cyclone nest from ships that approach too closely.
loreCanon.values: Nest, storm eye, and access to carrion or dropped food.
loreCanon.folklore: Iron hook feet, vulture wings, and rigging attacks are true. Punishing-soul imagery is a mortal interpretation of predation.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: Frozen seas forced Harpies into storm corridors and ships; First Cracks made warm currents and shipping lanes more crowded.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native storm beast. A Wyrd mutation may make a flock target memories rather than bodies, but Harpy is not Wyrdspawn.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether Harpies have a social alarm language that sailors can learn to avoid a nest.

folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Harpy (Greek mythology):** The "snatchers"  -  bird-women spirits of sudden storm-winds who stole food from their victims and carried off the souls of the dead. They were agents of divine punishment.; **Asanbosam (West African/Ashanti folklore):** A vampire-like creature with iron teeth and hook-like feet that dwelt in forest canopy, dangling its legs down to snatch prey from below.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Mast-Snatcher:** Harpys perch in the rigging of Iceheart ships, snatching crew members directly from the decks. They use their hook-feet to grip masts and yardarms, dangling upside-down to reach into hatches and cabins. A ship under Harpy attack must be abandoned or reach port within hours. **The Storm-Rider:** They nest in the eyes of perpetual storms, riding the updrafts. They are the only creatures that can navigate an Iceheart cyclone without disorientation. Merryn sailors consider seeing a Harpy a death-omen  -  but also a navigation aid, since the creatures always fly toward the storm's calmest exit-corridor.

creatures.name: Hippocampus
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Hippocampus
creatures.origin: The Hippocampus is inspired by the pre-Binding sea-horse that drew the Wave-Lord's chariot, combined with the salt-depth tradition of the Jengu, a water-spirit associated with healing, prophecy, and coastal boundaries. In this setting, they serve as the loyal mounts of the Myrathil.
creatures.nature: Appearing from the chest up as a powerful horse with an arched neck, intelligent eyes, and a flowing mane of kelp, the creature's lower body transitions into a serpentine, fish-scaled tail that coils through the water. Its coat matches the blue-green of coastal waters, countershaded pale underneath. The kelp mane is bioluminescent, glowing green in the deep, while its hooves are modified into steering fins. Its noble face features liquid eyes that change from calm blue to storm green or moonlit silver.
creatures.habitat: These creatures reside in the brackish estuaries, coastal harbors, and shallow shoreline waters of the Iceheart Sea.
creatures.combat: 130 HP. Rideable (special: can be tamed and ridden by Myrathil divers; land speed 30, swim speed 60; saddle naturally forms from kelp). Wave-Crest (passive: can calm or raise waves in a 30-ft radius, granting allies +10 swim speed and making water difficult for enemies). Estuary-Purify (passive: presence purifies Wyrd-tainted water; creatures drinking from Hippocampus-tended water are immune to water-borne disease for 24 hours). Kelp-Mane-Glow (passive: bioluminescent mane provides light in 20-ft radius). Hoof-Fin-Steer (melee, +4 to hit, 1d6+2 bludgeoning). Vulnerable to poison.
creatures.depth: Capable of outpacing storm-currents, Hippocampuss are tamed by Myrathil divers to patrol the harbors of Merrowport. Their presence naturally purifies Wyrd-taint from coastal waters, protecting nearby settlements from water-borne diseases and plagues. They are drawn to the boundaries where fresh rivers meet the sea. A local keeper has reported that a wild Hippocampus has been spotted nearby, and the local temple is looking for adventurers to help guide it safely to a contaminated estuary.
hooks: A rumor spreads of a Hippocampus spotted near the area.
Adventurers need a component from a Hippocampus to complete their quest.
creatures.description: A noble creature combining horse and serpent, this gentle elemental purifies waters and serves as a swift steed.
creatures.heritage: This native water-horse predates the Great Binding. Derived from pre-Binding sea-horse myths and salt-depth water-spirit beliefs, the Hippocampus represented the hope of finding safe passage and calm winds on open water. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It clears toxins, guides Myrathil divers, and chooses whether a human vessel has earned a harbor escort

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Hippocampus rather than creates it: a native water-horse lineage that purifies brackish boundaries and travels between coast and open sea; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native water-horse lineage that purifies brackish boundaries and travels between coast and open sea.
loreCanon.function: It clears toxins, guides Myrathil divers, and chooses whether a human vessel has earned a harbor escort.
loreCanon.values: Clean water, young, and the living edge between river and sea.
loreCanon.folklore: Horse-serpent form, kelp mane, healing, and harbor patrol are true. Its Wyrd-purifying effect is native function, not Wyrd origin.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding froze estuaries; First Cracks and warm runoff created refuges where the kind could continue breeding.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native purifier and Wyrd-resistant. Wyrd may target or hunt it, but Hippocampus is not Wyrdspawn.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Define whether purification is digestion, symbiosis, or a water-bound spiritual office.

folkloreInspiration.primaryMyth: Hippocampus (Greek mythology) & Jengu/Mami Wata variant (West African/Sawa tradition)
folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Hippocampus (Greek mythology):** The sea-horse of the gods  -  a creature with the upper body and forelegs of a horse and the lower body of a fish or serpent. They drew Poseidon's chariot across the waves.; **Jengu/Mami Wata variant (West African/Sawa tradition):** A beautiful water-spirit  -  a mermaid-like being whose hair and body are always wet, associated with healing, prophecy, and the boundary between fresh and salt water.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Wave-Steed:** Hippocampuss can be tamed and ridden by Myrathil divers. They are the fastest mode of underwater transport in the Iceheart  -  capable of outpacing storm-currents. Breakers-Born Myrathil use them to patrol the harbor-approaches of Merrowport. **The Estuary-Guardian:** They are drawn to the brackish boundary where fresh-water rivers meet the salt sea  -  the River-Fed Myrathil's territory. Their presence purifies water contaminated by Wyrd-taint, making them essential to the health of coastal settlements. A village with a resident Hippocampus never suffers from water-borne plague.

creatures.name: Gorgon
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Gorgon
creatures.origin: This creature combines the pre-Binding Gorgon, whose hair of snakes and terrible face turned onlookers to stone, with the salt-depth myth of the Adze, a vampiric firefly-spirit that drinks blood and shifts between insect and humanoid forms. In the deep sea, she is a dread entity of the trenches.
creatures.nature: She appears as a serpentine humanoid woman with skin the deep violet of the abyss and a lower body composed of coiling sea-serpents. Her hair is a writhing mass of tiny, glowing, bioluminescent eels that pulse in hypnotic, rhythmic patterns. Translucent scales cover her torso, revealing dark veins. Her face is frozen in an expression of eternal rage, dominated by solid, glowing green eyes that cause the blood of onlookers to crystallize with calcium. She carries a mirror of polished abalone.
creatures.habitat: This creature makes its home in the dark, freezing waters of the abyssal trenches within the Iceheart Sea.
creatures.combat: 380 HP. Stone-Gaze (ranged 30 ft, DC 15 SPI or progressive petrification begins � round 1: -10 speed; round 2: restrained; round 3: petrified; gaze must be maintained). Eel-Hair-Hypnosis (passive: bioluminescent eel-hair pulses hypnotically; DC 13 SPI or entranced, can be pulled toward her without resistance). Firefly-Shift (1 AP: compresses into a single tiny bioluminescent eel, becoming nearly invisible � DC 16 INT (Perception) to spot; in this form she drinks blood from fish). Abyssal-Mirror (special: polished abalone mirror reflects gaze attacks back at attackers; once per round as a reaction). Vulnerable to radiant.
creatures.depth: The petrifying gaze of the Gorgon leaves living statues of terror on the sea-floor, which are often animated by the Wyrd to plague shipping lanes. She can compress her body into a single, tiny bioluminescent eel to slip through fishing-nets and drain the blood of captured catches. To prevent this, sailors must inspect their catch with silver mirrors, which expose her disguise.
