creatures.origin: Cursed by the tragic fate of the Thalren Vourdalak, a vampire that targeted its own grieving family, and the madness-inducing Vedic Pishacha, a dark horror of the cremation grounds, the Vourdalak-Debt represents the horror of unresolved obligations. In Mythrill, they are the restless dead driven to sustain their false lives through the vitality of their kin.
creatures.nature: This figure appears almost exactly as it did in life but with too-pale skin, stiff movements, and a smile that is too wide, dressed in peat-stained burial clothes. Peat-black liquid flows through its visible, translucent veins, and it carries the cracked contract-tablet that recorded its debts in life. Its face is frozen in its final moment of terror or fading, though its eyes remain fully aware and screaming at the horror of its state.
creatures.habitat: This tragic revenant wanders the damp settlements within the Bryngloom Forest terrain.
creatures.combat: 285 HP. Death-Eater (passive: feeds on the bodies of the dishonored dead; each corpse consumed restores 20 HP). Corpse-Plague (passive: where it feeds, disease spreads; any creature that eats food or drinks water from an area where the Rat-Father has fed must DC 14 CON or contract a disease). Death-Whisper (passive: can detect the exact moment of death for any creature within 100 miles). Rat-Swarm (passive: commands all rats within 1 mile; can summon them as a swarm dealing 2d6 piercing per round). Regeneration (regenerates 10 HP per round while corpses are present). Vulnerable to radiant (radiant damage stops regeneration and deals double damage).
creatures.depth: Known as the Debt-Revenant, the Vourdalak-Debt is returned to a half-life by the Morvane to complete its broken Neth or Vreken contract, draining its family's life force to do so. It also acts as a Madness-Speaker, possessing blood relatives to speak secrets of contract loopholes and buried artifacts, making these encounters a desperate search for Neth weavers and adventurers seeking to free the family from the spirit's parasitic bond or to retrieve a component from it.
hooks: A rumor spreads of a Vourdalak spotted near the area.
Adventurers need a component from a Vourdalak to complete their quest.
creatures.description: A tragic revenant returned to its family, the Vourdalak-Debt drains the life of its loved ones to sustain its broken contract.
creatures.heritage: This native family-bound revenant form tied to unresolved grief and contract predates the Great Binding. Rooted in vampire legends that target their own families, the Vourdalak represented the ultimate fear of domestic decay, wasting sickness, and family betrayal. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It returns to loved ones, drains life to prolong an obligation, and can recognize a family member who honestly confronts the debt

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Vourdalak-Debt rather than creates it: a native family-bound revenant form tied to unresolved grief and contract, not automatically a Wyrd vampire; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native family-bound revenant form tied to unresolved grief and contract, not automatically a Wyrd vampire.
loreCanon.function: It returns to loved ones, drains life to prolong an obligation, and can recognize a family member who honestly confronts the debt.
loreCanon.values: Family claim, unresolved promise, and the continuity of a broken household.
loreCanon.folklore: Familiar appearance, too-wide smile, life drain, and debt-revenant behavior are true. The record's Morvane intervention needs a specific rule.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding made blood and contract obligations binding across generations; First Cracks worsened settlement isolation and family debt.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native death-form under review. A Wyrd version may possess a corpse, but do not make all Vourdalak Wyrdspawn.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether the revenant can be released by restitution, mourning, legal cancellation, or only destruction.

folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Vourdalak (Slavic/Russian folklore):** A vampire of Russian and Slavic tradition  -  specifically, a vampire that returned to its own family, pretending to be alive, while slowly draining the life of its loved ones. The vourdalak was particularly tragic because it preyed on those who mourned it most.; **Pishacha (Hindu/Vedic mythology):** A flesh-eating demon of Hindu tradition  -  a creature of darkness, disease, and madness that dwelt in cremation grounds. Pishachas could possess the living, causing insanity, and were said to speak in languages that predated human speech.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Debt-Revenant:** Vourdalak-Debts are the Bryngloom's most common and most pitied creatures. They are Neth or Vreken who died with unfulfilled contract-obligations  -  the Morvane has returned them to a half-life, bound to complete the terms of their broken contracts. They return to their families, appearing alive, and slowly drain vitality from their loved ones to sustain their own false existence. **The Madness-Speaker:** Like the Pishacha, it can possess the living  -  but only those who share its bloodline. A possessed family member speaks in the Vourdalak's voice, revealing secrets the dead person knew: contract-loopholes, hidden debts, the location of buried artifacts. The Neth consider Vourdalak-possession both a curse and a source of critical intelligence  -  the dead see contractual implications the living cannot.

creatures.name: Mavka-Willow
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Mavka
creatures.origin: The Mavka-Willow draws from the Thalren Mavka, a forest spirit of a woman who died unnaturally, beautiful from the front but hollow-backed with visible organs, combined with Sol's Breath Yakshini, tree-spirits bound to sacred growth who could bless or curse travelers. In the woodlands of Mythrill, they represent the alluring, deceptive beauty of the wilderness.
creatures.nature: From the front, this spirit appears as a stunningly beautiful woman with pale-green leaf-like skin, willow-bark hair, and bare feet merging with the roots, wearing a dress of leaves sewn with spider-silk and smelling of willow-sap. From behind, she has no back or spine, but rather a hollow cavity filled with rustling leaves and wooden organs. Her exquisite face is marked by spring-green eyes and parted lips, carrying a heartbreakingly innocent expression.
creatures.habitat: This tree-bound nymph lives at the roots of ancient trees in the Bryngloom Forest terrain.
creatures.combat: 130 HP. Night-Kiss (melee, +5 to hit, 1d6+3 psychic � a kiss from Nott inflicts vivid nightmares on the target; DC 14 SPI or gain 1 level of exhaustion). Dark-Veil (passive: where she passes, darkness follows; all creatures within 30 ft have disadvantage on Perception checks). Shadow-Ride (passive: rides across the sky in a chariot drawn by black horses; each hoofbeat dims the light for 100 ft). Dream-Seal (passive: can seal a creature's dreams, preventing divination and prophetic dreams for 24 hours). Vulnerable to radiant (radiant damage dispels the darkness aura).
creatures.depth: Acting as a Tree-Bride, each Mavka-Willow is bound to a specific willow whose growth reflects her mood, which the Neth monitor as a living archive since the tree's rings store her memories. Her dangerous Hollow-Back Secret draws onlookers to walk around her, only to be driven mad by the sight of her hollow interior, though the Vreken have learned a funeral chant to force her to turn away. Adventurers might be hired to protect Neth researchers or to harvest components from the Mavka's sacred tree.
hooks: A rumor spreads of a Mavka spotted near the area.
Adventurers need a component from a Mavka to complete their quest.
creatures.description: A beautiful, leaf-clad dryad of the willows, the Mavka-Willow hides a hollow back and a mind-shattering secret.
creatures.heritage: This native willow-bound tree person predates the Great Binding. Born from legends of women who died unnaturally, the Mavka served as a comforting explanation for untimely deaths, imagining them as beautiful forest spirits. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It tends a specific willow, stores memory in rings, and can bless or punish those who use the tree

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Mavka-Willow rather than creates it: a native willow-bound tree person whose front/back duality records life, death, and hidden root memory; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native willow-bound tree person whose front/back duality records life, death, and hidden root memory.
loreCanon.function: It tends a specific willow, stores memory in rings, and can bless or punish those who use the tree.
loreCanon.values: Its tree, ring memory, and the boundary between beautiful public story and hidden bodily truth.
loreCanon.folklore: Leaf-clad woman, hollow back, and tree-bride bond are true. The horror is a native body truth, not Wyrd design.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: Cold preserved ring records; First Cracks altered willow growth and made certain trees living archives.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native tree person. Wyrd can hollow or impersonate a Mavka, but the kind is not Wyrdspawn.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether the willow chooses the Mavka or the Mavka is born from the tree's accumulated memory.

folkloreInspiration.primaryMyth: Mavka / Navka (Slavic/Ukrainian folklore) & Yakshi / Yakshini (Hindu/Vedic mythology)
folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Mavka / Navka (Slavic/Ukrainian folklore):** A forest-nymph  -  the spirit of a child or young woman who died an unnatural death. Mavky appeared as beautiful young women from the front, but had no back  -  their internal organs visible from behind. They dwelt in forests and waterways, luring young men to their deaths.; **Yakshi / Yakshini (Hindu/Vedic mythology):** Tree-spirits of Hindu tradition  -  benevolent or malevolent beings connected to specific trees. Yakshini were often depicted as voluptuous women standing at the base of sacred trees, granting boons to the worthy and curses to the unworthy.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Tree-Bride:** Each Mavka-Willow is bonded to a specific ancient willow-tree in the Bryngloom. The tree's health reflects her mood  -  when she is content, the tree flourishes; when she grieves, it withers. The Neth catalog every Mavka-tree as a protected living-archive node, because the trees serve as memory-storage: each ring of the trunk contains a year of the Mavka's observations. **The Hollow-Back Secret:** Her most devastating power is the compulsion to circle behind her  -  those who see her front feel an overwhelming urge to walk around and see her back. When they do, the sight of her hollow, organ-visible interior drives them mad. The only protection: never approach a Mavka-Willow from any angle. The Vreken have developed a specific chant  -  a list of names of the dead  -  that, when sung, causes the Mavka to turn away first, breaking the compulsion.

creatures.name: Alkonost
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Alkonost
creatures.origin: The Alkonost is derived from the Thalren Alkonost, a bird of paradise whose song brought total joy and oblivious peace, merged with Sol's Breath Gandharvas, celestial musicians who guarded sacred soma and inspired involuntary devotion. In Mythrill's damp canopy, she plays a sacred melody that captures the light of dawn.
creatures.nature: Boasting a twenty-foot wingspan, this bird has the head, arms, and torso of a beautiful woman, with shifting rose, gold, violet, and blue plumage. She plays a sacred lute that vibrates with the resonance of creation, weaving ribbons of golden light through the canopy while causing flowers to bloom on dead wood. Her face has perfect symmetry and glowing skin, with eyes holding the colors of the dawn and a beatific smile that has never known pain.
creatures.habitat: This celestial musician makes her home in the high branches of the Bryngloom Forest terrain.
creatures.combat: 130 HP. Lying-Voice (passive: speaks in the voice of the target's most trusted person; DC 14 SPI or charmed for 1 round). Truth-Reversal (special: reverses the meaning of spoken words � a vow of protection becomes a vow of destruction, a curse becomes a blessing; DC 15 SPI or the reversal takes effect). Silver-Tongue (passive: words are silver; its lies sound more convincing than the truth; +4 to Deception). Mind-Maze (passive: creates false scenarios in the target's mind � DC 13 SPI or confused for 1d4 rounds). Vulnerable to radiant.
creatures.depth: Known as the Joy-Singer, her song induces a state of euphoric oblivion, making it tempting to the contract-laden Neth. However, she is also a Memory-Thief, as every minute spent listening erases a year of the listener's past; these erased memories are stored in her dawn-colored feathers, which Vreken crypt-scholars seek to harvest for their secrets, offering a lucrative but highly dangerous task for adventurers who are hired when sightings are reported or when a specific component is needed.
hooks: A rumor spreads of a Alkonost spotted near the area.
Adventurers need a component from a Alkonost to complete their quest.
creatures.description: A beautiful bird of paradise whose heavenly song brings total joy at the cost of the listener's memories.
creatures.heritage: This native joy-singer and canopy musician predates the Great Binding. Derived from paradise bird myths whose song brought oblivious joy, the Alkonost represented the hope of finding peaceful escape from the harsh cold of the forest. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It offers relief from pain, tests whether listeners consent, and chooses whether to leave a listener with joy or dangerous oblivion

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Alkonost rather than creates it: a native joy-singer and canopy musician whose song alters memory and emotional state; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native joy-singer and canopy musician whose song alters memory and emotional state.
loreCanon.function: It offers relief from pain, tests whether listeners consent, and chooses whether to leave a listener with joy or dangerous oblivion.
loreCanon.values: Song, pleasure, and the right to choose whether one remembers suffering.
loreCanon.folklore: Bird-woman body, heavenly song, euphoric oblivion, and memory cost are true. The song is not automatically a Wyrd attack.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding made escape from hardship more tempting; First Cracks altered canopy acoustics and brought more desperate listeners.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native song being with possible Wyrd-amplified memory theft. Keep distinct from Wyrdspawn and from Sirin.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Differentiate Alkonost as joy/oblivion, Gamayun as knowledge, and Sirin as grief or final rest.

folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Alkonost (Slavic folklore):** A bird of paradise from Russian folklore  -  a creature with the head and chest of a beautiful woman and the body of a bird. Her song brought joy and the forgetting of all sorrow. Those who heard her sing forgot everything they had ever wanted and lived in a state of contented oblivion.; **Gandharva (Hindu/Vedic mythology):** Celestial musicians and guardians of the gods  -  divine beings who presided over sacred music, marriage ceremonies, and the soma-ritual. Gandharvas were so beautiful that their appearance could cause involuntary devotion.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Joy-Singer:** The Alkonost's song causes total joy-oblivion  -  listeners forget every sorrow, every grief, every loss, and exist in a state of euphoric contentment for as long as the song continues. The Neth, who carry centuries of accumulated memory and the weight of the First Contract, find the Alkonost's song almost irresistible  -  the prospect of forgetting everything is a form of liberation. **The Memory-Thief:** The danger: the joy is purchased with memory. Each minute of listening permanently erases a year of memory. A Neth who listens for ten minutes loses a decade. The Velun arcanists have determined that the Alkonost's erased memories are not destroyed but woven into its dawn-colored feathers  -  plucked and read by Vreken crypt-scholars, they contain the most intimate secrets of the forest's most powerful beings.

creatures.name: Dziwozona-Wild
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Dziwozona
creatures.origin: The Dziwozona-Wild stems from the Polish Dziwozona, a wild, green-haired swamp-nymph who drowned men and swapped infants, and Putana, the Vedic demoness who posed as a wet-nurse to poison the baby Krishna. In Mythrill's wetlands, she represents the cruel archetype of the false-mother who preys on grief.
creatures.nature: Standing seven feet tall, this massive, barrel-chested woman has wild green hair dripping with bog-water and large breasts that leak a luminescent fluid. Her skin resembles waterlogged grey-green wood, with webbed hands and feet, and she carries a swaddled bundle of stolen memories wrapped in Neth silk. Her face is flat and frog-like, featuring nose-holes, a wide mouth, and small pig-like eyes, though she can project an illusion of beauty that can fool even Neth truth-sense.
creatures.habitat: This deceptive swamp-dweller resides in the pools and rivers of the Bryngloom Forest terrain.
creatures.combat: 75 HP. Thought-Mirror (passive: reflects the target's deepest fear as a mental image; DC 14 SPI or Frightened 1 round). Memory-Feast (passive: devours memories; each memory consumed restores 5 HP). Shadow-Eye (passive: flies ahead of its master, scouting; can communicate with its master telepathically up to 10 miles). Truth-Eye (passive: sees through all illusions and lies; +10 to Insight checks). Vulnerable to radiant.
creatures.depth: Acting as the False-Mother, she offers poisoned milk to grieving parents to put them into a permanent sleep before leaving a changeling of woven bog-grass in their place. Her actual amphibious offspring, the Substitute-Children, are left in human cradles and grow rapidly while devouring contract-paper, forcing Neth households to hunt these creatures down and retrieve their stolen kin before their archives are destroyed, providing a desperate hook for adventurers.
hooks: A rumor spreads of a Dziwozona spotted near the area.
Adventurers need a component from a Dziwozona to complete their quest.
creatures.description: A grotesque water-woman who projects illusions of beauty, the Dziwozona-Wild targets families to swap children for ravenous changelings.
creatures.heritage: This native wild water mother or changeling predator predates the Great Binding. Rooted in Polish swamp-nymph myths, the Dziwozona was a warning story explaining infant changelings and why newborns sometimes fell sick. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It protects an amphibious brood, tests grieving parents, and exchanges or steals children according to an old reproductive practice

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Dziwozona-Wild rather than creates it: a native wild water mother or changeling predator associated with pools, milk, and the danger of false nurture; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native wild water mother or changeling predator associated with pools, milk, and the danger of false nurture.
loreCanon.function: It protects an amphibious brood, tests grieving parents, and exchanges or steals children according to an old reproductive practice.
loreCanon.values: Brood, water territory, and a harsh conception of survival through substitution.
loreCanon.folklore: Green hair, poisoned milk, false beauty, and changeling exchange are useful but disturbing records. The story is not a universal Wyrd origin.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding made infant survival and household memory more precarious; First Cracks created warm breeding pools and increased settlement overlap.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native/hybrid review. A Wyrd impostor may copy a false mother, but the native kind must be defined separately.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether child exchange is literal breeding behavior, a rare individual crime, or a metaphor for the creature's adoption of abandoned young.

folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Dziwozona / Mamuna (Slavic/Polish folklore):** A wild, ugly water-woman of Polish tradition  -  a creature with excessively large breasts, a flat face, and green hair who lurked in rivers and lakes, drowning men and substituting her own ugly children for human infants.; **Putana (Hindu/Vedic mythology):** A demoness sent to kill the infant Krishna by offering him her poisoned breast-milk. Krishna drained her life-force through her own breast, killing her and freeing the souls she had trapped. Putana represents the archetype of the false-mother.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The False-Mother:** She appears to families who have lost children, offering comfort  -  her poisoned breast-milk induces a deep, euphoric sleep from which the drinker never wakes. She then substitutes a "changeling"  -  actually a bundle of woven bog-grass that superficially resembles the sleeping victim, ensuring the family does not search for the real one until it is too late. **The Substitute-Child:** Her own offspring  -  ugly, amphibious creatures with her flat face and webbed digits  -  are left in human cradles in place of stolen infants. These substitutes grow at an alarming rate and develop an insatiable appetite for contract-paper. A Neth household that discovers a Dziwozona-changeling must act quickly  -  the creature grows one foot per day and will consume the entire household archive within a week if not removed and returned to the bog.

creatures.name: Upir-Root
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Upir
creatures.origin: The Upir-Root draws from the ancient Thalren Upir, a blood-drinking vampire blamed for blighted fields and agricultural ruin, combined with the parasitic Vedic Bhuta, a restless spirit that anchored itself to the soil to drain the vitality of the living. In Mythrill's depths, it manifests as a literal blight upon the forest's hydrology.
creatures.nature: This creature appears as a skeletal, underground network of dark tendrils that spread from a central burial point, mimicking ironwood roots but pulsing with a slow heartbeat. Where they touch living roots, they leech nutrients to wither the tree above. At the center of the network, buried six feet deep, lies the original peat-preserved corpse with its eyes open, its mouth stretched in a silent scream, and root-tendrils sprouting from its mouth, eyes, and fingertips.
creatures.habitat: This parasitic entity spreads beneath the soil of the Bryngloom Forest terrain.
creatures.combat: 650 HP. Blood-Root (passive: feeds on the blood of the living; its body is a network of blood-vessels that extend into the ground like roots). Life-Force-Drain (melee, +6 to hit, 2d6+4 necrotic + DC 14 CON or lose 1d4 CON permanently). Blood-Control (special: can control any creature that has drunk its blood; the controlled creature must DC 16 SPI or obey the Upir's commands for 1 hour). Regeneration (regenerates 15 HP per round; only radiant damage stops regeneration). Blood-Scry (passive: can see through any creature that has its blood in its veins � an entire spy-network). Sunlight-Weakness (passive: takes 2d6 radiant damage per round in direct sunlight). Vulnerable to radiant.
creatures.depth: Operating as a Root-Parasite, the Upir-Root drains the life force of everything within a fifty-foot radius, causing trees to yellow and inducing severe fatigue in Neth travelers walking above. As the primary Blight-Cause in the forest, these infestations are targeted by the Neth Velun using contract-rituals to legally release the spirit's attachments, though adventurers are often needed to locate the buried center of the network or protect the ritualists from the spirit's defensive tendrils, especially if a component from the core is required.
hooks: A rumor spreads of a Upir spotted near the area.
Adventurers need a component from a Upir to complete their quest.
creatures.description: An underground network of pulsing, parasitic tendrils, the Upir-Root drains the life of the forest and travelers above it.
creatures.heritage: This native subterranean root parasite predates the Great Binding. Derived from ancient Slavic vampire beliefs blamed for agricultural ruin and blighted crops, the Upir represented the fear of invisible soil blights. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: It drains or redistributes vitality, controls a root territory, and may be negotiated with when a grove is dying

creatures.loreNote: Folklore records Upir-Root rather than creates it: a native subterranean root parasite associated with blood, blighted fields, and the forest's reciprocal life flow; its pre-Binding baseline remains independent of the Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A native subterranean root parasite associated with blood, blighted fields, and the forest's reciprocal life flow.
loreCanon.function: It drains or redistributes vitality, controls a root territory, and may be negotiated with when a grove is dying.
loreCanon.values: Root territory, stored life force, and the balance between growth and consumption.
loreCanon.folklore: Pulsing tendrils, blighted fields, fatigue, and root-parasite behavior are true. It is not created by Wyrd fear.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding changed decay and growth cycles; First Cracks warmed root channels and made the parasite's range more active.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Native blight ecology under review. Wyrd may overfeed or weaponize one network, but Upir-Root is not automatically Wyrdspawn.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether the Upir-Root is a single network intelligence or many organisms connected through the forest.

folkloreInspiration.primaryMyth: Upir / Upyr (Slavic folklore) & Bhoot/Bhuta variant (Hindu/Vedic mythology)
folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Upir / Upyr (Slavic folklore):** One of the earliest Slavic words for vampire  -  a revenant that rose from the grave to drink blood. Upirs were particularly associated with root-crops and agriculture, blamed for blighted harvests and withered fields.; **Bhoot/Bhuta variant (Hindu/Vedic mythology):** Drawing from the darker aspect of Bhoot lore  -  a restless, earth-bound spirit that fed on the vitality of living things, draining not through bites but through proximity, like a metaphysical parasite anchored to the soil.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Root-Parasite:** Upir-Roots are the parasitic underground networks of those who died with such intense attachment to a place or person that their bodies refused to decompose. Their root-tendrils drain the vitality of every living thing in a fifty-foot radius  -  trees yellow and drop their leaves, animals sicken, and Neth who walk above feel an inexplicable exhaustion. **The Blight-Cause:** Entire sections of the Bryngloom canopy have been killed by Upir-Root infestations  -  trees that should live for centuries wither and die within a single season. The Neth Velun have developed specific contract-rituals to sever an Upir-Root's attachment: a formal legal declaration of release, spoken into the soil above the corpse, that acknowledges the dead person's desire and formally declares it fulfilled. If the declaration is sincere and legally sound, the roots crumble to peat within hours.

creatures.name: Sirin-Song
creatures.illustrationCaption: A hand-drawn field sketch of the legendary Sirin
creatures.origin: The Sirin-Song represents the dark Thalren Sirin, whose beautiful but sorrowful song led listeners to willingly cease living, combined with the nine cosmic forces Sol's Breath faith calls the Navagraha, that dictate the path of destiny. In Mythrill's deepest forest, she acts as a tragic weaver of fate and a harbinger of the end.
creatures.nature: Having a twenty-foot wingspan, this bird-like entity has the head and upper torso of a gorgeous woman, with dark twilight plumage of indigo, violet, and black shot with silver threads. Her song projects ribbons of shadow that dim all light and drop the temperature, while she holds nine silver threads representing the aspects of fate. Her face is the most beautiful in the world, permanently still with eyes closed to hide the overwhelming sight of all time, her lips constantly moving to hum her terrible, perfect song.
creatures.habitat: This mournful singer resides at the convergence of the bog and forest in the Bryngloom Forest terrain.
creatures.combat: 380 HP. Soul-Song (passive: its song contains the final words of every dead person � the last thing they said before dying; the song changes continuously as new people die). Sorrow-Aura (passive: creatures within 30 ft must DC 14 SPI or gain 1 level of exhaustion from overwhelming grief). Death-Prophecy (passive: its song foretells the manner of death for everyone within hearing range; the prophecy is always accurate). Song-of-Death (passive: those who hear the full song die of heartbreak within 24 hours � only those with strong willpower (SPI 16+) can resist). Healing-Tears (passive: weeps tears of light that can heal wounds and cure diseases; 2d6 radiant healing to one creature per round). Vulnerable to necrotic.
creatures.depth: Performing the Death-Song at the forest's deepest core, her voice is the sound of the Morvane, driving listeners to sit down and peacefully surrender to the swamp. As the Fate-Weaver, she manipulates nine threads representing elements like birth, contract, and dissolution to shape destinies, prompting the Neth to avoid her at all costs and providing a legendary challenge for any adventurers who dare seek her tears or seek to alter a predetermined doom, or if a sighting prompts a high-stakes investigation.
hooks: A rumor spreads of a Sirin spotted near the area.
Adventurers need a component from a Sirin to complete their quest.
creatures.description: A dark bird of twilight with a heart-breaking face, the Sirin-Song sings a melody of absolute melancholy that pulls listeners toward their final rest.
creatures.heritage: This native creature predates the Great Binding. Rooted in dark bird-of-paradise legends, the Sirin represented the personification of deep, overwhelming sorrow that drove listeners to surrender their lifelines. This being was already there; these stories recorded encounters with a creature that existed long before the Great Binding, not one created by mortal fear or the Wyrd.

loreClassification.agency: a native singer that draws listeners toward grief, release, or final rest

folkloreInspiration.description: Inspired by **Sirin (Slavic folklore):** A dark counterpart to the Alkonost  -  a bird-woman whose song brought not joy but sorrow and death. Those who heard the Sirin's song were overcome with such profound, beautiful melancholy that they simply stopped living  -  not from violence, but from an inability to return to ordinary existence after hearing perfection.; **Navagraha / Nine-Spirit (Hindu/Vedic astrology):** The nine celestial influencers of Hindu tradition  -  nine cosmic forces that shape destiny through their positions and movements. Combined with the Sirin, this creates a creature whose song weaves the threads of fate itself, pulling listeners toward their predetermined end.
folkloreInspiration.settingAdaptation: **The Death-Song:** The Sirin-Song sings at the deepest, darkest heart of the Bryngloom  -  the point where the forest, the bog, and the Sunken Spire converge. Her song is the sound of the Morvane itself  -  the audible expression of the cosmic force that decides what the forest preserves and what it consumes. Those who hear it do not die  -  they simply choose to stop. They sit down, close their eyes, and allow the bog to take them, willingly, gratefully. **The Fate-Weaver:** Her nine silver threads connect to the nine forces that shape every creature's destiny in the Bryngloom: birth, debt, love, betrayal, contract, silence, threshold, dissolution, and return. By plucking a single thread, she can alter a person's fate  -  extending a life, calling a debt early, or triggering a dissolution. The Neth Velun arcanists believe the Sirin is the Keeper's voice  -  the mechanism through which the Last Threshold communicates its will. They do not seek her out. They pray they never hear her song.

creatures.name: Grandmother of the Bog
creatures.illustrationCaption: An ancient, moss-covered hag standing in a dark peat-pool, holding a wooden spoon
creatures.origin: The Grandmother of the Bog is an ancient fey entity born from Thalren peat-bog folklore. She offers extensions on life to dying mortals in exchange for their most precious memories.
creatures.nature: A massive, moss-covered hag standing over seven feet tall, wrapped in peat-moss and willow roots. Her eyes are glowing amber points, and she carries a wooden spoon and a pot of boiling bog-soup.
creatures.habitat: Widow's Quagmire, peat-bogs, and willow groves of the Bryngloom Forest.
creatures.combat: 380 HP. Memory Loan (ranged, DC 15 SPI or lose 1 memory; targets take 3d6 psychic). Peat Graft (heals 20 HP/turn when standing in bog water). Peat Curse (slows all targets in 30-ft area). Vulnerable to fire.
creatures.depth: She is a master negotiator, signing contracts that grant travelers safety in the bog but leave them unable to recall their childhoods. The soup she boils is made of memories and bog-lichen.
hooks: A grieving sister traded her memory of her brother to the Grandmother in exchange for his survival from a peat-collapse.
The players need to retrieve a memory from the Grandmother's soup-pot to solve a succession crisis in Atropolis.
creatures.heritage: Born from ancient Thalren folklore of swamp-hags trading lifetimes for memories.
creatures.description: An ancient, moss-covered bog-hag that trades years of life for travelers' memories.

loreClassification.agency: It negotiates, preserves travelers in bog soup, and grows stronger when people surrender identity for time

creatures.loreNote: Folklore translates Grandmother of the Bog's Collector/judge and mimic/interpreter function rather than creates it: this ancient cosmic Wyrdkin persists through Peat pools, willow roots, memory-rich soup, and contracts signed near Widow's Quagmire and is not assumed to be Keth-Amar's offspring.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: An ancient cosmic memory-and-lifespan trader that adapted to Bryngloom bog law; it is not necessarily a post-Keth creation of local folklore.
loreCanon.function: It negotiates, preserves travelers in bog soup, and grows stronger when people surrender identity for time.
loreCanon.values: The memory-for-life exchange, its contract network, and the continuity of the cosmic colony around its lair.
loreCanon.folklore: Moss hag, life extension, memory payment, soup, and safe-passage terms are local translation and tactical warning. Native bog crones are not automatically this entity.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding made lifespan and memory politically valuable; First Cracks warmed peat and supplied living material and contracts the arriving trader could exploit.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Ancient Cosmic Wyrdkin proposed; direct Keth-spawn memory trader remains an open alternative.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether bargains can be reversed, whether lost years can return, and whether the cosmic trader can be expelled rather than merely out-negotiated.
loreCanon.cosmicProvenance: Working hypothesis: a Between collector that exchanges stored memory, potential, or biological time between organisms and nests.
loreCanon.wyrdFunction: Collector/judge and mimic/interpreter; it turns cosmic exchange into familiar bog bargaining and targets desperate travelers.
loreCanon.anchor: Peat pools, willow roots, memory-rich soup, and contracts signed near Widow's Quagmire.
loreCanon.kethRelationship: Keth-Amar can exploit its bargains to drain identity from Bryngloom, but the Grandmother may be an independent trader with separate interests.
loreCanon.independence: It can negotiate and expand its contract web after Keth-Amar retreats; it may have local clients, rivals, or a faction that rejects his hunt.
loreCanon.countermeasure: Expose hidden terms, restore surrendered memories, use native contract witnesses, and sever the bog's contract web without damaging the natural water cycle.

creatures.name: Debt-Revenant
creatures.illustrationCaption: A peat-preserved corpse in rusted scale armor, rising from the marsh holding a contract
creatures.origin: When a Neth debtor dies with unfulfilled contract obligations, their spirit is denied rest by the Neth pacts, rising as a peat-revenant to complete the terms of their agreement.
creatures.nature: A peat-preserved corpse clad in rusted Neth scale-armor and wrapped in rotting peat-bonds. Its eyes glow with a cold, blue light, and it carries the contract that binds it in its chest cavity.
creatures.habitat: Peat-bogs, marshlands, and scriptorium ruins of the Bryngloom Forest.
creatures.combat: 290 HP. Peat Grip (melee, +6 to hit, 2d8+4 physical + target is restrained). Binding Oath (melee, target cannot cast spells until they move 30 ft away). Rise from Bog (resurrects at 50% HP after 2 rounds unless decapitated). Vulnerable to radiant.
creatures.depth: It cannot rest until its contract is legally fulfilled or the document is burned by a Neth pact-mage. It is intensely hostile to anyone who attempts to block its path or salvage its armor.
hooks: A pack of Debt-Revenants is attacking a peat-cutting camp, claiming the workers are violating an ancestral compact.
The players must find a loophole in a Debt-Revenant's contract to lay it to rest before it destroys a village.
creatures.heritage: Derived from the fear of Neth debt collectors returning after death to claim outstanding payments.
creatures.description: A peat-preserved undead debtor that rises to complete the terms of a broken Neth contract.

loreClassification.agency: It follows a written obligation, attacks obstruction, and tries to complete a contract that no living authority can now interpret

creatures.loreNote: Folklore translates Debt-Revenant's local form rather than creates it: this direct Keth-spawn depends on Contract documents, peat-preserved corpses, scriptorium ruins, and Neth/Vreken obligation records, and it can follow its clause without active commands, but it likely cannot reproduce unless new documents and corpses are exposed to Wyrd.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A likely direct Wyrd manifestation occupying a dead debtor or contract corpse; an ancient cosmic corpse-parasite stage is not ruled out, but the local body is the leading answer.
loreCanon.function: It follows a written obligation, attacks obstruction, and tries to complete a contract that no living authority can now interpret.
loreCanon.values: The literal contract, the corpse's unfinished identity, and the document or clause anchoring it.
loreCanon.folklore: Peat-preserved body, rusted Neth armor, contract bonds, and burning the document are local translation and tactical tells.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding created blood-oath precedent; First Cracks made Neth/Vreken debt systems more intrusive and supplied dead paperwork and bodies for a later Wyrd body.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Direct Keth-spawn / Wyrdspawn proposed, pending the cosmic parasite comparison.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether native Neth law can release it or whether the Wyrd has made the contract legally counterfeit, and settle direct spawn versus cosmic parasite.
loreCanon.cosmicProvenance: Unknown. The form could be a Keth-generated larva using a corpse, or a cosmic debt parasite whose normal life cycle is being translated through Neth paperwork.
loreCanon.wyrdFunction: Parasite/sower and collector/judge; it turns a dead obligation into a contagious legal pressure on the living.
loreCanon.anchor: Contract documents, peat-preserved corpses, scriptorium ruins, and Neth/Vreken obligation records.
loreCanon.kethRelationship: Direct Wyrd generation is the leading hypothesis because the form literalizes a local contract during the Wyrd era; ancient cosmic provenance remains open.
loreCanon.independence: It can follow its clause without active commands, but it likely cannot reproduce unless new documents and corpses are exposed to Wyrd.
loreCanon.countermeasure: Fulfill or lawfully cancel the obligation, burn the anchor document, cleanse the corpse, and prevent the Wyrd from transferring the clause to another debtor.

creatures.name: Cycle-Eater
creatures.illustrationCaption: A grotesque, worm-like creature with insectoid limbs, feeding on a glowing willow root
creatures.origin: The Cycle-Eater is a grotesque aberration born from the fear that Keth-Amar will devour the forest's reincarnation cycle entirely. It crawls beneath the marshes, feeding on the roots of sacred willows.
creatures.nature: A massive, worm-like horror with multiple insectoid limbs and a circular mouth lined with needle-like teeth. Its body is covered in a glowing, purple slime that drains magic from the surrounding area.
creatures.habitat: Deep peat-pools, hollow roots, and convergence shrines of Bryngloom.
creatures.combat: 400 HP. Devour Cycle (melee, +7 to hit, 3d8+5 necrotic; target cannot be resurrected/healed for 3 rounds). Cycle Aura (passive aura, 20 ft: healing spells cast in area are reduced by 50%). Void Burst (ranged, 2d10 void). Vulnerable to fire.
creatures.depth: It feeds on the life-force of dying creatures, preventing their spirits from returning to the loop of rebirth. A grove occupied by a Cycle-Eater slowly turns grey and sterile, its trees unable to bud.
hooks: A sacred willow grove is dying, and the local Druids believe a Cycle-Eater is nesting in the roots.
The players must retrieve the glowing slime of a Cycle-Eater to craft a ward against necrotic magic.
creatures.heritage: Born from the fear that Keth-Amar will consume the forest's rebirth cycle entirely.
creatures.description: A grotesque worm-like aberration that devours the reincarnation cycle of the forest and prevents healing.

loreClassification.agency: It feeds on dying life, prevents return to the forest cycle, and sterilizes a grove so recurrence becomes absence

creatures.loreNote: Folklore translates Cycle-Eater's Drainer/harvester, parasite/sower, and independent cosmic predator function rather than creates it: this ancient cosmic Wyrdkin persists through Deep peat, hollow roots, convergence shrines, dying creatures, and any Wyrd breach touching the rebirth cycle and is not assumed to be Keth-Amar's offspring.

loreCanon.trueOrigin: A possible ancient cosmic predator that feeds on death-rebirth cycles, or a direct Keth-spawn shaped by fear that Keth-Amar will consume Bryngloom's renewal. It is not native to the forest.
loreCanon.function: It feeds on dying life, prevents return to the forest cycle, and sterilizes a grove so recurrence becomes absence.
loreCanon.values: Its feeding tunnel, the interrupted cycle, and the Wyrd pressure that makes loss permanent.
loreCanon.folklore: Worm body, insectoid limbs, circular mouth, sterile grove, and blocked rebirth are local translation and tactical warning. Native death-rebirth ecology predates it.
loreCanon.bindingEffect: The Binding and First Cracks changed decay and growth cycles but did not create the organism; warm root convergence gives either cosmic fauna or direct spawn more life to consume.
loreCanon.wyrdRelationship: Ancient Cosmic Wyrdkin versus direct Keth-spawn review.
loreCanon.nextDecision: Decide whether a grove can be healed while consumed spirits remain recoverable, whether the creature has a single core, and whether it predates Keth-Amar's arrival.
loreCanon.cosmicProvenance: Working hypothesis: a Between drainer that hunts regenerative ecologies around living worlds and consumes recurrence as a form of nourishment.
loreCanon.wyrdFunction: Drainer/harvester, parasite/sower, and independent cosmic predator; it weakens Morvane/Root-Veil boundaries whether or not Keth-Amar commands it.
loreCanon.anchor: Deep peat, hollow roots, convergence shrines, dying creatures, and any Wyrd breach touching the rebirth cycle.
loreCanon.kethRelationship: Keth-Amar can direct it toward Bryngloom to stop renewal, but it may be an independent predator whose goals only overlap with his hunt.
loreCanon.independence: It can remain and feed after Keth-Amar retreats, potentially becoming a local faction or solitary apex organism with no interest in leaving.
loreCanon.countermeasure: Restore the native cycle, sever the root network, protect dying life from harvest, and close the breach sustaining the worm.
